### Fix: a roster split across two chat messages by an LLM output cutoff was silently truncated to the tail-only message ([ADR-0110](docs/adr/0110-roster-continuation-message-merge.md))

Contact-form report: customer said generating her mystery cut her 22-character list to 16. She hadn't actually generated yet — no `mystery_packages` row existed for any of her conversations. Traced to the concept chat itself: her reply asking to swap in her own 22-character cast got cut off mid-sentence after character 16 (LLM output limit), and when she asked it to continue, the AI sent characters 17-22 as a *separate* message headed "... - CONTINUED". `findLatestConceptMessage()` always resolves to the single chronologically-latest assistant message that independently parses a roster — the continuation message's header breaks the strict header regex (trailing "- CONTINUED" text), so it falls to the header-agnostic batch parser, which still parses its own 6 characters (17-22) as a complete, standalone roster. Verified by extracting the real regex/logic into a standalone script and running it against her actual messages: **had she hit Generate, she'd have gotten 6 characters, not 16 and not 22** — worse than what she reported, and not yet shipped to any customer.

Fixed by adding `mergeRosterContinuations()`: before any extraction runs, fold a message whose roster starts numbering above 1 (e.g. "17." not "1.") onto the end of the assistant message immediately preceding it. Real rosters always start at 1, so this is a safe structural signal — no from-scratch replacement list is ever misidentified as a continuation. Wired in once, at the top of `extractCharactersFromMessages()`, so the `approvedMessageId` lookup, the primary header parser, and the secondary bold-line fallback all inherit the fix. Verified against the customer's actual conversation before/after: before the fix, extraction resolves to 6 characters; after, it resolves to all 22 with no name collisions between the two halves. Deployed and confirmed live via `get_edge_function`.

Also flagged, not fixed here: the concept chat itself fabricated a specific, wrong technical claim ("the system has a maximum character limit... typically 16") when it didn't actually know the backend's behavior, then retracted it unprompted one message later. Worth a follow-up to the chat's system prompt so it doesn't assert backend limits it can't verify.

### Fix: `parse-claude-json` couldn't recover a clean but unclosed JSON response, silently zeroing out a well-formed character's guilty-branch content ([ADR-0103](docs/adr/0103-new-purchase-coherence-sweep-ritual.md) Addendum 3)

Root-caused the last open item from today's sweep incident: Cypress/Celine Beaumont's guilty-branch content (`round2_guilty` through `final_guilty` + `reveal_confession_guilty`) came back empty across two separate generation attempts. Pulled the actual failing Claude response via the Make API's execution log — `stop_reason: "end_turn"`, only 2360 of 5000 available `max_tokens` used, ruling out truncation entirely — but the JSON was genuinely malformed: the last field ended on a complete, well-formed sentence with no closing `"` or `}` anywhere after it. Claude simply stopped without closing the structure it was still inside, despite the prompt explicitly instructing it to verify closure before emitting. Since `parse-claude-json`'s parse is all-or-nothing, this single formatting slip zeroed out all 5 fields from that call, even though 4 of the 5 were already complete and well-formed at the point generation stopped.

Fixed by adding a new, deliberately conservative final sanitization stage (`attemptCleanTrailingCutoffRecovery`): detects being stuck inside an open JSON string at end-of-input where the trailing text ends on sentence-terminal punctuation (`.`/`!`/`?`), and closes the string plus any remaining open braces/brackets before retrying the parse. Deliberately does *not* recover a messier, mid-word/mid-sentence cutoff — that shape is far more likely a genuine `max_tokens` truncation, and silently "closing" it would ship a visibly cut-off sentence instead of correctly falling through to the existing empty-field handling the missing-content detectors and auto-recovery loop already cover safely. Verified against the actual real failing payload (extracted via the Make API, not reconstructed by hand) before deploying: recovers all 5 fields correctly; a synthetic mid-word truncation and normal valid JSON both still behave exactly as before. Deployed (`parse-claude-json` v10, `verify_jwt` preserved as `true`) and re-verified both cases directly against the live endpoint post-deploy.

Not done: Cypress's own character row on the original package wasn't backfilled (moot — her guilty branch is never used, per the detective_script fix in the same ADR). No historical sweep run for whether this exact shape has quietly affected other characters/packages before now, silently absorbed by the existing 2-attempt auto-recovery retry.

### Fix: found and closed the actual source of the ADR-0108 incident — Make.com's Parent blueprint calls a Postgres function that was blind to missing character rows ([ADR-0109](docs/adr/0109-get-empty-characters-blind-to-missing-rows.md))

Follow-up to today's ADR-0108 fix. Pulled the live Make.com blueprints via the Make API (`MAKE_API_TOKEN`) to find what actually performed the unguarded completion write ADR-0108 traced — ruled out the Child scenario (writes only to `mystery_characters`), found it in the live Parent scenario ("Parent60"): a router writes `generation_status='completed'` when a prior HTTP module's result is empty, and that module calls the `get_empty_characters` Postgres RPC directly. That function can only ever return rows that *exist* — a wholly-missing character (no `mystery_characters` row at all) is invisible to it by construction, exactly reproducing today's incident. A prior migration comment claimed this function was "never wired into any caller" — true of this repository (confirmed via grep), false of the live system; the caller's entire definition lives in Make.com's UI, invisible to any repo-based search.

Fixed by extending the function with an additive branch that returns one synthetic sentinel row when actual character count is short of the expected roster size (reusing the already-trusted `package_expected_character_count()` parser from ADR-0094/0095) — makes Make.com's existing "is the result empty?" check correctly see a missing character, with no Make.com blueprint edit or manual import required. Verified in an isolated `BEGIN...ROLLBACK` test before deploying: reconstructed the incident (catches it, previously returned 0 rows) and confirmed no false positive on a genuinely complete package. Confirmed via grep that nothing else in this codebase calls this function directly, and that Make.com's only check (array length) doesn't care about the sentinel row's `NULL` id.

ADR-0108's trigger fix remains the safety net regardless — this closes the actual source so the self-heal path shouldn't need to fire for this specific cause going forward, but the trigger still catches it if it ever does.

### Fix: completion trigger only validated the first completion attempt, letting a fourth write path silently ship a package short a character ([ADR-0108](docs/adr/0108-completion-gate-must-revalidate-every-write.md))

Follow-up to today's sweep fix ([ADR-0103](docs/adr/0103-new-purchase-coherence-sweep-ritual.md) Addendum 2). Traced why Jaclyn's package shipped `completed` (firing the ready email) while genuinely missing a character, despite the existing row-count guard (ADR-0094/0095) being verified correct against this exact package's live data. Neither of the two cron functions that guard protects ran within minutes of the package's actual completion write (confirmed via `cron.job_run_details`), and no edge function in the repo performs that write either — pointing to a fourth, unguarded write path (almost certainly Make.com's Child scenario blueprint writing "batch finished" directly). `validate_package_characters()`'s trigger only fires on `generation_completed_at`'s *first* NULL→NOT NULL transition and permanently no-ops for that package afterward, so it never got a second look.

Fixed by broadening the trigger to re-validate on *every* transition of `generation_status` into `completed`, from any source — same guard logic already inside the function, just no longer one-shot. Closes the gap regardless of which system performs the write, without touching Make.com's blueprint. Deployed live, verified both that the function definition changed and that the behavior actually works: an isolated `BEGIN...ROLLBACK` test (throwaway conversation/package/character, 1 of 2 expected characters present, simulated rogue completion write) confirmed the trigger correctly intercepts and downgrades to `needs_review` — then rolled back with zero footprint on real data.

Also considered and deliberately skipped a client-side mirror check (character count vs. expected) originally proposed alongside this fix — the reveal gate's own code comment documents "trust the server's completed guarantee" as the deliberate design, and duplicating that check client-side would reintroduce the paired-predicate-drift shape this codebase has been burned by before. The broadened trigger is comprehensive enough (fires on every `UPDATE`, any caller) that there's no remaining gap for a client-side copy to catch.

Notably, this directly revisits a tradeoff the prior ADR (ADR-0094) explicitly discussed and declined at the time, calling the risk "a hypothetical future third path" — this incident is that path turning out to be real four days later.

### Fix: post-purchase coherence sweep on "Operation: Thirty & Murdery" — detective_script hardcoded a fixed culprit in a slip-draw package, plus a missing character row ([ADR-0103](docs/adr/0103-new-purchase-coherence-sweep-ritual.md) Addendum 2)

Sweep on Jaclyn's 30-player, has-accomplice purchase (conversation `624ad4af-3b5b-43d8-8f25-7df919ef153f`) found a real guardrail violation: `detective_script`'s reveal section named a specific murderer ("Dr. Kai Okonkwo") and accomplice ("Dr. Westley Kimura") by name, even though this is a `mystery_style='character'` slip-draw package where G8 (`docs/generation-guardrails.md`) requires no character be designated guilty anywhere — everything else (game_overview's "randomly selected at game time" line, every character's full innocent/guilty/accomplice branches, `character_role='suspect'` for all 30) was correctly built for the random-slip mechanic; only the detective's own scripted reveal broke it. `list_packages_with_slip_culprit_leak()` returned zero hits and doesn't catch this shape — it only scans characters' static secret fields for confession phrasing (the original "Adelaide Crane" incident), never `detective_script` itself for a named fixed culprit.

Fixed directly, zero-cost text edit (no Anthropic call): rewrote the reveal's culprit-naming sentences to the same host-fill-in bracket convention already used elsewhere in the document (`**[GUILTY PLAYER'S NAME]**` / `**[ACCOMPLICE PLAYER'S NAME]**` with explicit stage directions). Verified no hardcoded names remain and the edit doesn't trip the meta-text-leak detector's bracket markers.

Also found and fixed: Cypress/Celine Beaumont had no `mystery_characters` row at all despite `generation_status` already reading "completed" — the completion gate only validates existing rows, so a wholly-missing character doesn't block completion, and the "ready" email had already gone out before the gap was caught. The package had also dropped out of the automatic `needs_review` retry loop once it (incorrectly) reached "completed." Manually re-fired the same recovery webhook the automated system uses; the row was created but her guilty-branch round content came back empty across two attempts (the automated 2-attempt cap is now exhausted, possibly the same content-filter-block class as the Sylvie/Sylvain Dubois precedent). Left as-is — the reveal fix means her guilty branch is never actually used in this package's delivered gameplay.

Not done: no new detector built for the "fixed culprit in detective_script" shape, no corpus-wide sweep for other live packages with the same pattern. Full detail and rationale in the ADR-0103 addendum.

### Fix: purchase preview wrongly said "not ready" for a concept whose roster was split into "###" subsections

Customer (Jaclyn, 30-player "Operation: Thirty & Murdery," 5 masterminds + 24 manipulated guests) reported the chat said her concept was locked in and ready, but clicking Generate showed "not ready." Root cause was purely client-side, in `parseCharacters()` (`src/pages/MysteryPurchase.tsx`): the section-terminator regex `(?=##|$)` used to find the end of the `## Character List` section matches `##` as a *substring*, so it stopped at the very first `### The Five Masterminds` subheading — exactly where her roster began, since her plot naturally split the cast into "masterminds" vs "innocents" subsections. `characterSection` came out effectively empty, `parsedDetails.characters.length` was 0, and the ADR-0044 "don't take payment for a mystery that doesn't exist" guard fired, blocking purchase entirely. No `mystery_packages` row existed for this conversation — she was blocked before ever reaching backend generation.

This is the same paired-predicate-drift shape as ADR-0055/56/57: `mystery-webhook-trigger`'s `extractRosterFromMessage()` (the real post-purchase extraction gate) was *already* hardened to tolerate `###` subheadings between roster entries, but that fix was never ported to this client-side preview twin, so the two disagreed on whether her concept was complete.

Fixed by extracting the existing header-agnostic whole-message scanner (already used when no header matches at all) into a shared `scanWholeMessageForRoster()` helper, and falling back to it whenever the header-scoped patterns find zero characters — not just when no header was found. Verified against a reconstruction of her actual message content (30 numbered `**Name** – description` entries split across two `###` subsections): before the fix, `characterSection` extracted to a blank string and 0 characters parsed; after the fix, all entries parse correctly. Verified no regression against a normal flat (no-subsection) roster. No backend/edge-function changes — this was purely a client-side parser gap.

Not yet investigated: her concept message is also byte-identical across all 3 generations at exactly 8162 characters, truncated mid-sentence on character #30 with no closing sections — likely a `max_tokens` ceiling on the concept-chat completion call for large (30-player) rosters. Didn't block this incident (the parser failed before reaching that point) but worth a follow-up if a customer's roster itself comes back incomplete rather than just unparseable.


### SEO: internal-link authority pass from the weekly digest's 3 action prompts (corporate page, homepage, template-guide page)

Acted on 3 of the weekly SEO/GEO digest's action prompts (week ending 2026-08-24): the corporate/office page (417 impressions, pos 18.5, near-zero CTR — an authority problem per the digest, not a copy one), the homepage's custom-* buyer queries (locked title/meta per ADR-0024/0046, so links not copy), and the rising "murder mystery template" query (14 impressions, +14 WoW, pos 7.6).

Verified against live content before touching anything (one suggested link — `ai-murder-mystery-generator-complete-guide` → homepage — already existed from earlier work; skipped re-adding it). Also found the digest's assumption wrong in one place: the homepage H1 ("Create Murder Mystery Parties in Minutes") does not contain "custom" at all — only the locked `<title>`/meta does. Left the H1 untouched (out of scope for this pass, flagged for Jonathan).

Shipped 4 link insertions + 1 new on-page section, applied durably via `cross_link_map.json` (new `insertions` entries, `target_page` field per the ADR-0023 landing-page convention) and mirrored live to `blog_posts.content` via a surgical Supabase `UPDATE` (not a full `backfill-crosslinks` run — matches the ADR-0023 precedent of a version-controlled durable source plus a small-blast-radius immediate write):
- `murder-mystery-party-for-corporate-events`: self-links its own first-sentence "office murder mystery party" mention → `/office-murder-mystery-party/` (pos 48.2, was getting zero internal links).
- `ai-generated-murder-mystery-vs-prewritten-kits` → homepage (`/`), anchor "custom murder mystery party" (this post had no homepage link at all).
- `free-murder-mystery-games-printable` → `murder-mystery-party-script-template-guide`, anchor "murder mystery template".
- New section on `murder-mystery-party-script-template-guide` ("Want a Murder Mystery Template Without Building One Yourself?"), targeting the bare "murder mystery template" phrase (the page's own H1/intro didn't use it) and linking to `/mystery/create`.
- Homepage (`src/pages/Index.tsx`, support section): added 2 new outbound lines to the corporate post and template-guide post, matching the existing "Browse our free murder mystery templates" line's style.

Deliberately skipped one digest-suggested link (`free-murder-mystery-games-printable` → corporate post): that post never mentions offices, teams, or corporate contexts anywhere, and forcing an unrelated sentence in to carry the link would have been worse than not linking — Jonathan confirmed skip over drafting new unrelated copy.

Not done: the German "krimidinner 30 personen" and rising "corporate murder mystery" query watch items, and the ADR-0046 canonical-consolidation re-measurement (`node scripts/backfillSeoHistory.mjs jul2026_custom_page_canonicalization`) — both flagged in the same digest but out of scope for this pass; re-check in next week's digest.


### Improvement: drafted the pipeline-level fix for the victim dual-name defect below — decide the victim's name once, at generation time ([ADR-0107](docs/adr/0107-victim-single-name-decided-at-generation.md))

Follow-up to the data fix below: traced why the "Margot/Marc Dubois"-style leak happens at all. Neither the concept chat (`mystery-ai/index.ts`) nor the Make.com Parent blueprint's `master_context` prompt actually instructs the gender-flexible "Name1/Name2" naming convention anywhere — the model generates it unprompted for every named person, suspect and victim alike, and nothing has ever told it the victim (never played by a guest) is a different case from a suspect (always played by one). That's why whether the parent-generation stage (`game_overview`/`detective_script`) and child-generation stage (`evidence_cards`/characters) agree on the victim's name is essentially chance. Checked for downstream breakage first: `adapt-mystery-apply`'s reassignment logic and the `package_victim_is_playable_character()` detector both only ever expand *suspect* names, never the victim's — safe to remove the victim's dual-name entirely. Added an explicit instruction at the exact point `victimProfile.name` gets defined, across all 4 Part 1 prompt variants (detective/character × murder/intrigue): murder-style victims get a flat "decide ONE single name, never the A/B format" rule; intrigue's "wronged party" (which — unlike a murder victim — can sometimes be a playable character) gets a conditional version instead. Character/suspect dual-naming is untouched — that's an intentional, unrelated product feature. Drafted as `Parent59 (Victim Single-Name Decision)`, built on `Parent58` (re-confirmed as the actual current head via `temp-files/` first, since another concurrent session landed it today — not built on the stale `Parent57` this investigation started from). Superseded same day by `Parent60 (Wait Before Completion Check)`, landed by a separate concurrent session on top of Parent59 — confirmed all 4 victim-naming insertions carried forward intact, so `Parent60` (not `Parent59`) was the actual import candidate. **Imported and confirmed live same day**, verified directly via the Make.com API (scenario `9106101`: `isActive: true`, live `/blueprint` response contains all 4 instructions) rather than just trusting the import — actually serving new webhook calls now, not just uploaded.

Also added a defense-in-depth SQL detector (`supabase/migrations/20260823_detect_unresolved_victim_dual_name.sql`, deployed): `list_packages_with_unresolved_victim_name()` flags any completed package whose `master_context.victimProfile.name` still contains "/". Verified against the live corpus — correctly caught the 5 known offenders (the 3 patched today, plus 2 more found while widening the check: Ghosts Of The Past; The Masked Betrayal, neither showing the customer-visible parent/child disagreement, left as-is). Read-only, not wired into the completion-blocking gate (no validated zero-false-positive run yet). Wired into `CLAUDE.md`'s sweep checklist as a third detector alongside the existing two. Full rationale, including why the prompt fix is additive (there was no prior rule to correct) rather than a fix to something that was wrong, in the ADR.

### Fix: victim's dual-gender placeholder ("Margot/Marc Dubois") leaked into evidence cards and character content on 3 live packages, invisible to both automated detectors ([ADR-0104](docs/adr/0104-close-post-purchase-free-regeneration-hole.md) Addendum 3, [ADR-0103](docs/adr/0103-new-purchase-coherence-sweep-ritual.md) Addendum 1)

A repeat sweep on Toby Wragg's already-"resolved" purchase (*Death On The Île De Ré*) found that this morning's Addendum 2 claim of "victim name consistent" was wrong: `game_overview`/`detective_script` had resolved the victim to `"Margot Dubois"`, but `evidence_cards` and all 4 characters' background/secrets/accusations still carried the raw dual-gender placeholder `"Margot/Marc Dubois"` straight from `master_context`. Neither `list_packages_with_meta_text_leak` nor `list_packages_with_victim_mismatch` catch this — both check for the victim's name *appearing*, and `"Margot"` is a substring of `"Margot/Marc"`, so they read as clean. Checked whether this was isolated to Toby's package (which had a rocky, manually-triggered generation history) — it wasn't: sampled 11 live completed packages with a detectable dual-name victim, found 3 affected (27%), including two more already-delivered customer packages fixed the same session: **Behind The Mask: Death At The Gilded Circle** (12 of 15 characters carried `"Reginald/Regina Vandermere"` against a resolved `"Reginald Vandermere"` everywhere else) and **Death At The Velvet Rose** (a single leftover `"Vivienne/Victor Ashford"` in `game_overview`'s opening line, against `"Victor Ashford"` used consistently everywhere else). All 3 fixed via targeted SQL substring replacement matching each package's own already-resolved name, re-verified clean on both detectors plus a full re-scan for the raw placeholder string. Root cause (not fixed here — data-only fix, no pipeline change): whichever generation stage, parent or child, resolves the victim's dual-gender placeholder to a single name does so independently, with no shared resolution passed between them. ADR-0103's sweep checklist (step 4) updated to require exact-string comparison across documents instead of substring-presence checking, and to flag that dual-gender placeholders are the intentional default for every named character (including the victim) — not, by themselves, a leak.

### Fix: purchase tracking fired duplicate GA4 events with a hardcoded (wrong) value + wired real Google Ads purchase conversion
Found while implementing the Ads "Purchase" conversion event: `stripe-webhook/index.ts` already sends an accurate server-side GA4 purchase event via Measurement Protocol on every real party purchase (real `session.amount_total`/`currency`/`payment_intent`), but `PaymentSuccess.tsx` was *also* firing a second, separate client-side GA4 `purchase` event (`trackPurchaseComplete()` in `analytics.ts`) with a hardcoded `value: 24.99` and `transaction_id` set to the conversation ID rather than the real Stripe payment intent. Since the two events used different transaction IDs, GA4 had no way to deduplicate them — every purchase was almost certainly being double-counted in GA4 conversion/revenue reporting, with one accurate entry and one wrong-value entry, since launch. This predates the Ads work entirely; it just surfaced while building it.

Fixed: removed the client-side duplicate (deleted `trackPurchaseComplete` from `analytics.ts`, its only call site). Real per-purchase value now flows through cleanly: `stripe-webhook/index.ts` merges the confirmed `amount_total`/`currency`/`payment_intent` into `conversations.mystery_data.payment` (deploy v67, verified live, `verify_jwt` preserved as `false`) instead of the client having to guess which of the two real price points ($24.99 full, $19.99 welcome-discount) applied. `PaymentSuccess.tsx` reads it back and fires the actual Google Ads "Purchase" conversion (`AW-18406526278/MxMoCN_-yeYcEMaa9chE`) with the real dynamic value/currency/transaction_id, guarded against double-fire the same way the old code was. Note: Google's own event-snippet template defaulted `currency: 'EUR'` (likely the Ads account's billing-country default, not the actual charge currency); this uses the real Stripe `session.currency` instead, which is USD for this product.

### Feature: single source of truth for the "your mystery is ready" email — DB-side half ([ADR-0106](docs/adr/0106-single-source-of-truth-ready-notification.md))
Follow-up to today's duplicate-email finding (Toby Wragg's purchase, ADR-0104 Addendum 2): the "Your Mystery is Ready! We'd Love Your Feedback" email lived as 12 duplicated HTTP modules inside the Parent Make.com blueprint, each behind its own "has empty characters → retry → recheck" sub-flow that raced against the separate, more careful `notify-generation-issue` recovery system without either knowing the other existed — causing the duplicate send and roughly doubling generation time/spend on any package that hit an initially-empty character (confirmed via Make's dead-letter queue: Sylvie/Sylvain Dubois's round-content call was blocked by Anthropic's content filter, and the resulting recovery race is what padded Toby's generation to ~20 minutes and 8 Child-scenario executions instead of the usual ~10-11 minutes and ~4-5). Shipped the DB-side half: new `ready_email_sent_at` column on `mystery_packages`, a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger (`notify_package_ready()`) that fires exactly once on the genuine transition into `generation_status.status = 'completed'` regardless of which code path caused it, and a new `send-mystery-ready-email` edge function it calls. Verified live against an existing `is_test` package (no real customer touched): confirmed the trigger fires and calls the function on the first transition, confirmed a second transition to `completed` does *not* re-fire (checked `net._http_response` — no second request queued, `ready_email_sent_at` unchanged), then reset the test row. Not yet done: the Parent blueprint still has all 12 duplicate email modules and the retry sub-flows live — removing those (the other half of the fix) is being prepared as a new versioned blueprint (`Parent57`) for review before publishing, since it touches the live revenue-critical generation path and can't be fully dry-run without a real purchase.

### Feature: Google Consent Mode v2 + cookie banner for EEA/UK/CH traffic ([ADR-0105](docs/adr/0105-consent-mode-v2-eea-cookie-banner.md))
Closed the consent-gating gap flagged during the Google Ads base-tag install (below): GA4 and Google Ads previously fired unconditionally on all traffic, including confirmed real EEA sessions (Netherlands, Germany, France, Spain, Sweden, Italy, Denmark, Belgium, Austria). Added `gtag('consent', 'default', ...)` calls in `index.html`, before any `gtag('config', ...)` call — granted globally, denied specifically for the EEA + UK + CH `region` list (Google's own IP-based region detection decides who this applies to, not a home-grown geo-IP check; the site is a static GitHub Pages deploy with no server/edge layer available for that anyway). A new `ConsentBanner` component (`src/components/ConsentBanner.tsx`, `src/lib/consent.ts`) handles Accept All / Reject All / Customize (Analytics + Advertising toggles), persists the choice to `localStorage`, and calls `gtag('consent', 'update', ...)` accordingly; a synchronous reapply script in `index.html` re-applies a returning visitor's saved choice before the GA/Ads config calls run, so they aren't re-prompted or stuck denied every visit. Banner *visibility* (a separate, non-compliance-critical concern from the `region`-scoped defaults) uses a best-effort `Intl` timezone heuristic to avoid showing it to the ~91%-of-revenue US market; defaults to showing when detection is uncertain. Added a "Cookie Settings" reopen link to `Footer.tsx` and a new Cookies section to `Privacy.tsx`. Banner copy translated into all 13 locales (`consent` namespace + `footer.links.cookieSettings` in every `src/i18n/locales/*.json`), AI-translated rather than native-reviewed, same standing caveat as other localization work in this repo. Verified via Playwright against local dev: banner shows for a Berlin timezone and stays hidden for New York, Customize → toggle Analytics off/Advertising on → Save fires the correct partial `consent update` and persists, reload doesn't re-prompt and reapplies the saved state, footer link reopens the banner pre-filled with the saved choice. Full rationale (why `region` scoping over a geo-IP service, why timezone-only-for-visibility) in the ADR.

### Fix: normal customer generation flow was 100% broken since yesterday's ADR-0104 deploy — client self-collided with its own atomic claim on every attempt ([ADR-0104](docs/adr/0104-close-post-purchase-free-regeneration-hole.md) Addendum 2)
Found via the new-purchase coherence sweep (ADR-0103) on Toby Wragg's (toby.wragg@gmail.com) purchase, "Death On The Île De Ré." Package had zero content 20 minutes post-purchase — no characters, no game overview, no detective script — status `failed` with error "This mystery is already generating or has already been generated," `resumable: true` but retrying looped forever. Root cause: `mysteryPackageService.ts` wrote `generation_status: 'in_progress'` to the DB *before* calling `mystery-webhook-trigger`, which (as of yesterday's ADR-0104) atomically claims the row via `claim_package_for_generation()` and rejects with `409` if the row is already `in_progress` with a fresh `updated_at`. Since the client had just written exactly that one line earlier in the same call, every single generation attempt — first try or retry, no double-click or race needed — was guaranteed to self-reject. `generation_attempts` confirmed it: zero `claimed` outcomes from any client call since the ADR-0104 deploy (2026-08-22 ~17:45 CEST); the only successful claim in that window was a manual service-role call for a different customer (Eduardo Salgado, see yesterday's addendum below) — not the client recovering on its own. Only 2 paid purchases occurred in that window, so blast radius so far is small, but every future purchase would have hit this. Fixed: removed the client-side pre-write entirely; `claim_package_for_generation()` is now the sole writer of the `in_progress` state (it already creates the row if missing or claims an existing one), and `packageId` is resolved via a plain read after the edge function call instead. Verified the claim RPC runs before the `needs_more_info` concept-completeness gate in the edge function, so a package row always exists by the time later branches need `packageId`. Frontend-only change, no backend/edge function touched; typechecked clean. Toby's package was then manually triggered via a service-role call, generated successfully, and passed the full ADR-0103 sweep (victim name consistent, no meta-text/leak, no blocking defects). One character (Sylvie/Sylvain Dubois) initially came back missing round content and landed in `needs_review`; the existing `auto-remediate-held-packages` cron caught and backfilled it automatically within minutes, no manual intervention needed. Customer notified.

### Feature: installed Google Ads base tag (AW-18406526278) for the first Search campaign
Added `gtag('config', 'AW-18406526278')` to `index.html`, reusing the `gtag.js` loader already present for GA4 rather than adding a second script tag. ## 2026-08-22

### Fix: rate limiter counted harmless multi-tab race losses toward its budget, locking a paying customer out for an hour with zero content ([ADR-0104](docs/adr/0104-close-post-purchase-free-regeneration-hole.md) Addendum)
Found while running the new-purchase coherence sweep (ADR-0103) on Eduardo Salgado's (esj@salgados.net) second same-day purchase, "Veneno En La Medianoche" — the same customer as the reassignment incident above, unrelated code path, same day by coincidence. His purchase triggered `mystery-webhook-trigger`; 3 near-simultaneous calls (almost certainly two browser tabs racing the non-atomic client-side pre-check) each got a harmless `409` from ADR-0104's atomic claim guard — but the guard's rate limiter counted those 3 race losses as real attempts, exhausting the whole 3-per-60-minute budget before a single actual generation ever ran. Every subsequent call, including his own manual retries over the next 13 minutes, got `429`. Zero characters were ever generated for a $24.99 purchase. Compounding bug found in the same investigation: `mysteryPackageService.ts` hardcoded `resumable: true` and a generic "Failed to trigger generation" message for every non-2xx response — payment-required, already-in-progress, rate-limited, and genuine failures all looked identical, because `supabase.functions.invoke()` discards the status code and JSON body on error unless you explicitly read them off `error.context`. Fixed: (1) the rate limit now only counts `outcome = "claimed"` attempts — calls that actually won the claim and started a real, billable run — not race losses, which cost nothing and represent the same attempt as whichever call won; (2) the `429` response now carries `reason: "rate_limited"`; (3) the client now reads the real status/reason and sets `resumable: false` with accurate status text for rate-limited/already-generating rejections instead of blanket "resumable" framing. Deployed via `mcp__supabase__deploy_edge_function`, verified live (confirmed the deployed function's content matches source, not a stray placeholder from a first deploy attempt). Recomputed the customer's rate-limit count under the new logic — `0`, since none of his 31 attempts that day ever actually claimed — so the fix unblocked his conversation immediately with no manual cleanup. Manually retriggered his second package's generation via a service-role call once the fix was verified live; now `in_progress`. Full incident detail in the ADR addendum.

### Fix: murderer/accomplice reassignment never worked — 4 real bugs found and fixed on the first real customer use ([ADR-0088](docs/adr/0088-guest-dropout-multi-character-and-reassignment.md) Addendum)
Eduardo Salgado (esj@salgados.net) was the first customer ever to buy a "Remove a Character" murderer/accomplice reassignment — all 4 of his attempts failed (he paid twice, $10 total, after the first silent failure). Investigation (triggered by his contact-form message + the purchase notification) found this code path had never actually run against a real Anthropic key before today, despite shipping live on 2026-08-15. Three independent, all-reproducing bugs in the reassignment call itself, in `adapt-mystery-apply/index.ts`: (1) the reassignment call shared a 45s timeout with a much smaller polish-pass call — too short for its much bigger generation, every attempt died with "Signal timed out"; split into its own 120s `REASSIGN_TIMEOUT_MS`. (2) the post-write verify check compared the detective script against the promoted character's full `"Real Name - PlayerNickname"` composite string, which Claude's prose never reproduces verbatim — this rolled back an otherwise-correct write; fixed to check the real-name portion only. (3) `max_tokens: 8000` was an unvalidated guess that couldn't fit a full byte-for-byte `detective_script` + `evidence_cards_text` reproduction (required by the "only rewrite the naming sections" design) plus new content for a real 16-character package — both live attempts truncated at a consistent ~19,000-character offset; raised to `16000`, sized off that measurement. Deployed via CLI, verified live end-to-end: both reassignments (accomplice → Gaspar Mondragón, murderer → Carlota de Villaclara) completed clean, zero verify issues. Package data was never corrupted at any point during the failed attempts (writes only happen after generation succeeds). (4) Same-day follow-up: `polishWithClaude` (the smaller pre-reassignment polish pass) hit the identical truncation pattern on both successful runs at a ~9,250-character offset under its own `max_tokens: 4000` — never customer-visible since it degrades to deterministic-only output on any error by design, but the same class of bug. Briefly considered scaling `max_tokens` dynamically per-call off actual content length, then rejected it: Anthropic bills tokens generated, not requested, so there's no cost benefit to sizing down for a smaller batch, only a ceiling (16000) to stay under — and both calls already need close to it on a real package. Shipped the simpler fix instead: both calls now flatly request `max_tokens: 16000` and share one unified `ANTHROPIC_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (120s, replacing two separately-guessed timeouts), deployed without spending on another live test since a wrong guess there only ever degrades safely. Billing: the duplicate second charge was refunded; the first charge was deliberately held instead of refunded, then fulfilled for real once the fix was verified. Full incident detail in the ADR addendum.

### Fix: closed the post-purchase free-regeneration hole ([ADR-0104](docs/adr/0104-close-post-purchase-free-regeneration-hole.md))
Audit found the `completed`/`in_progress` guard against re-running generation was entirely client-side — `mystery-webhook-trigger`'s server side only checked `is_paid`, never generation status, and `verify_jwt` is disabled on it. Anyone holding a `conversationId` (which a customer already has, from their own persistent chat link) could call the edge function directly and re-trigger the full paid Make.com + Claude pipeline indefinitely, for free. Production data showed no evidence this had actually been exploited by a customer — every repeat-generation pattern found traced to a documented staff remediation — but the hole itself was real and reproducible. Fixed: added `claim_package_for_generation()`, an atomic conditional-`UPDATE` claim under a row lock (same shape as `claim_package_for_remediation`/ADR-0098's lost-ack-hardened claim), plus a new `generation_attempts` audit table backing a 3-attempts-per-hour rate limit independent of the status check. Service-role callers (staff remediation tooling) bypass both, unaffected. Verified live: a direct call against a real paid/completed conversation now returns `409` before touching Make.com, and a 4th rapid attempt returns `429` — zero real spend triggered by the verification itself.

### Fix: backfilled 2 completely-empty characters, found and fixed 4 real bugs in shared remediation tooling along the way ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md) Addendum 7)

### Fix: widened the sweep to full history (not just 5 weeks), caught a bug in my own patch, fixed 8 more packages back to Oct 2025 ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md) Addendum 6)
Jonathan asked whether to sweep further back since customers may not have played yet regardless of purchase date. Checked the data instead of guessing a window: 121 paid packages predate the Sonnet 5 upgrade (earliest from 2025-07-20, not just the last 5 weeks), 88 of those never had guest links sent to anyone. Re-ran the two patched detectors across full history instead of picking a calendar cutoff. In the process, caught a real bug in the patch shipped two hours earlier: PostgreSQL's regex flavor treats `\b` as a literal backspace character, not a word boundary (`\M` is correct) — the "per rules" marker had never actually matched anything in production. Also removed the `\[victim` marker entirely after finding it false-matched `[victim's name]`, a legitimate template token in fields the original validation pass hadn't checked. Both fixed directly. Re-running the corrected detector surfaced 8 more real, confirmed leaks (not newly exposed by the regex fix — the list was identical before/after minus the false positive) spanning 2025-10-23 through 2026-04-22: 7 packages with the same `[choose someone with...]` bracket-in-otherwise-good-accusation pattern (fixed by rephrasing just the bracketed clause, since the surrounding paragraphs were real evidence-specific content worth keeping), plus a leaked internal instruction in Murder At The TLC Reunion's `round4_innocent` field ("Reference the timeline from master_context"). One of the 8 (Death At The Birthday Bash, Jan 2026) already had its party — fixed anyway since the content is still live, but no customer action needed. Re-verified: both detectors now return zero hits across all of history except 2 known-legitimate false positives (a detective self-naming feature, not a bug). Full detail in the ADR addendum.

### Fix: swept 5 weeks of packages for the same defect family found in Lyn's mystery, fixed 6 more, patched both detectors that missed all of it ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md) Addendum 5)
Follow-up to yesterday's Lyn DiFranco content audit: checked whether the leaked-placeholder defect class was isolated or systemic. It correlates cleanly with the pre-2026-08-11 Haiku era (ADR-0074's blanket Sonnet 5 upgrade) — found and fixed the same defect family in 6 more packages, all created 2026-07-20 through 2026-08-04, zero hits in any of the 12 packages generated since the upgrade. Fixed: Death By High Tea (Phoenix Hart), Death At The Birthday Bash (Matt LeVora + Lindsay Stafford), Death At Château Buzancy (raw `[Accomplice name]`/`[murderer name]` tokens in the reveal script), The Enchanted Family Reunion Murder (dangling `[accomplice name, if applicable]` in a no-accomplice game), Death At Thornfield Manor (leaked `[ACCOMPLICE BEAT — Note...]` authoring note + Fitzwilliam Blackwood's relationships), and Birthday Betrayal In Hot Springs (Kiana/Dylan's accusations had leftover generic example text). Important nuance: `[MURDERER NAME]`-style brackets are sometimes *intentional* — two older slip-style packages use them deliberately as a host-fill-in-the-blank, since the culprit is drawn at the table — so a blind bracket-pattern sweep would false-positive on legitimate scripts. Patched both existing content-quality detectors (`supabase/migrations/20260822_patch_content_quality_detectors.sql`) which had returned zero hits the whole time despite all this — validated the new markers against full history first (caught and fixed one self-introduced false positive, "accomplice Beat" matching character name "Beatrix", before shipping). ### Fix: PostHog was never actually wired into the site's real deploy pipeline ([ADR-0102](docs/adr/0102-posthog-key-missing-from-actual-deploy-pipeline.md), supersedes [ADR-0100](docs/adr/0100-lost-posthog-project-recreated-without-recovery.md))
Following up on yesterday's "lost PostHog project" fix: after pointing Vercel's `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` at the new project and redeploying, a live check on mysterymaker.party (incognito, to rule out ad-blockers) showed zero requests to `i.posthog.com` — not even to a dead token, which would still fire. Traced it to the actual serving infrastructure: `curl -I https://mysterymaker.party` returns `server: GitHub.com`, matching the repo's `CNAME` (`www.mysterymaker.party`) — **the live site is served by GitHub Pages via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, not the Vercel project this whole investigation had been focused on.** That workflow's build step only ever passed `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`, and a hardcoded feature flag — `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` was never present in it at all, meaning `initPostHog()`'s `if (!isProduction || !POSTHOG_KEY) return` guard has silently no-op'd on every production page load since the integration was added 2026-04-24.
- This likely means PostHog never captured a single real production event, not just that 4 months of history was lost to a deleted project (ADR-0100's original theory, now unverifiable and moot either way).
- Fixed: added `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` as a literal value to `deploy.yml`'s build env (not a GitHub secret — PostHog project tokens are explicitly write-only/public-safe, same reasoning already established there for `VITE_ENABLE_GUEST_DROPOUT_ADAPTATION`).
- **Verified live**: pushed to `main`, GitHub Actions run completed clean, confirmed the new token is baked into the live production bundle (`curl` + grep), and a synthetic test event flipped the PostHog project's `ingested_event` flag from false to true. The pipeline is genuinely capturing events now, not just theoretically fixed.

### Fix: a health check silently undid a customer's paid character removal the day before her party — both detectors now know "gone" can mean "paid to remove it" ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md) Addendum 3)
Lyn DiFranco emailed again, hours after Addenda 1/2 shipped: her dashboard reverted to the 25-guest version, party tomorrow. - Confirmed the automated ADR-0097 recovery path did NOT fire (`auto_remediation_log` has zero rows for this package) — this was a human/agent acting in good faith on a misleading detector, not an unattended cron.

### Fix: found and fixed the actual root cause of the "Remove a Character" hang — a lost-acknowledgement race in the claim step ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md) Addendum 2)
Continuation of today's earlier systemic follow-up. With explicit owner sign-off (~$0.05–$0.25 approved Anthropic spend), built a throwaway test package and reproduced the hang live on the first attempt — on trivial 4-character test content, not just complex real-customer prose, ruling out content size/complexity as the cause.
- Root-caused precisely: the claim step's `UPDATE ... RETURNING` commits in Postgres, but its acknowledgement can fail to reach the running code, which then reads `claimed: null` and abandons a row it had, in fact, just claimed — silently, with zero writes, in well under half a second. This supersedes yesterday's "~150s platform wall-clock kill" theory, which was a reasonable inference from the *original* incident's multi-hour timeline but doesn't match the live reproduction (instantaneous, at the very first database call, no live backend connection ever running).
- Fixed: after a null claim result, one verification read now distinguishes "genuinely someone else's row" from "our own lost-acknowledgement write" (only the latter can produce a `processing_started_at` newer than when this attempt began) and proceeds as owner instead of abandoning it. Safe even in a worst-case double-execution: the pre-existing package-level claim (ADR-0088) is a second, independent lock, so at most one path can ever actually write.
- Verified the fix live: re-ran the same test row under the deployed fix — this time it ran 9.7 real seconds (an actual Anthropic call, not a 442ms fast-exit) and failed cleanly on an unrelated, expected test-data gap (`status: 'failed'` with a clear error, no orphaning) instead of hanging again.
- Also noted, not fixed (out of scope, harmless): the catch block sets `status: 'failed'` but never `completed_at` — a minor audit-trail gap for whoever next touches this function.
- All test data (conversation, package, 4 characters, adaptation row) cleaned up — zero remnants confirmed.

### Fix: checkout page defaulted non-English customers to English/USD-literal pricing at the moment of payment
Jonathan asked why accounts sign up in French/Spanish/etc. but purchases are ~100% English. DB investigation ruled out a bad chat experience — non-English conversations reach the same message-depth as English ones (comparable % hitting 8+ messages) — so the drop-off isn't during chat, it's between finishing the concept and paying: English converts at 12.6% (57/452 conversations), all non-English combined at 0.7% (1/141), and Spanish/Dutch specifically have 7-8 months of history at 0/41 and 0/22 — too large a gap to be explained by lower non-English traffic volume alone.
- Root cause in [MysteryPurchase.tsx](src/pages/MysteryPurchase.tsx): checkout redirects to a single hardcoded Stripe Payment Link with no `locale` param, so Stripe's hosted payment page fell back to browser auto-detection instead of the site's chosen language — a customer who chatted the whole concept in French could land on an English-only Stripe page to actually pay. The price itself was also hardcoded as literal `$24.99`/`$19.99` regardless of locale, and the `% OFF` discount badge text was never wrapped in `t()`, so it rendered in English on every non-English page.
- Fixed: `&locale=` now derived from `i18n.language` and appended to the Stripe URL (mapped against Stripe's actual supported-locale list, `zh-*` normalized to `zh`, unsupported codes fall back to `auto` — same as today's behavior); price display now uses `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' })` for locale-correct separators; added a `purchase.package.discountBadge` translation key (`{{percent}}% OFF` equivalent) to all 13 locale files.
- **Deliberately not done in this pass**: the actual charge stays USD for every locale — Stripe Adaptive Pricing / true multi-currency would need Stripe-dashboard-side product/price configuration, not just a code fix, so `Intl.NumberFormat` only fixes number formatting, not the currency itself. Also didn't verify whether EU payment methods (iDEAL, Bancontact, SEPA) are enabled on the Payment Link — that's Stripe-dashboard config, invisible from the repo. Also noticed in passing (pre-existing, unrelated to this fix): `da.json` and `sv.json`'s `purchase.package.priceDescription` is still the untranslated English string, not yet localized.
- New `discountBadge` translations for es/fr/de/ko/ja/zh-cn/nl/da/sv/fi/it/pt were machine-translated by Claude, not yet reviewed by a native speaker — same caveat as the rest of the localization work, flagged for the native-speaker verification pass Jonathan is already planning.

### Fix: systemic follow-up on the "Remove a Character" stuck-batch incident — 3 bugs ported to production, root-cause research, reclaim sweep drafted ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md))
Continuation of 2026-08-20's manual customer fix. Ported the two bugs found during that fix into the real deployed `adapt-mystery-apply` and redeployed: the word-boundary regex fix (bare surnames like "Cross" were matching inside unrelated words like "across") and the `secrets` array-shape fix (same real shape as `evidence_cards`, previously silently skipped).
- **Found a third, more serious bug while porting the other two**: one `variantRegex.test()` call in the file was the only one that didn't reset the regex's `lastIndex` afterward. Since the regex is global-flagged and reused across every later scan in the same invocation including verify, a stale `lastIndex` could make a later scan on a different string start mid-way through it and silently miss a real match — unlike the other two bugs (which only ever caused an unnecessary rollback), this one could in principle let a stale reference pass verify undetected. Fixed to match every other call site.
- Verified via `esbuild --bundle` before deploying; also fixed the file's stale "STAGING ONLY" header comment.
- Researched the original hang itself: Supabase's own docs/community threads describe a ~150s wall-clock cap on Edge Function requests that don't use `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil` for their main work (this function doesn't), and MDN notes `AbortSignal.timeout()`'s timer can be paused if the worker is suspended. Converged on a credible (not fully proven) theory: the platform kills the isolate abruptly around ~150s in, bypassing `try`/`catch`/`finally` entirely — which explains every symptom observed (no error, no chain-dispatch, indefinite stuck row) without needing `AbortSignal` itself to be broken.
- Drafted, then applied with explicit owner sign-off, `supabase/migrations/20260821_sweep_stuck_adaptation_batches.sql` — a `pg_cron` sweep that reclaims any `mystery_adaptations` row stuck in `processing` past its TTL, cause-agnostic (works regardless of why an invocation dies). Mirrors the existing `sweep_stuck_needs_review_packages` pattern. Per ADR-0092's policy (explicit owner sign-off required before any cron touches a paid-package table), presented it and got approval before applying — **confirmed live**: `cron.job` shows it scheduled every 10 minutes, active.
- Also caught and fixed a small housekeeping issue: the ADR's own filename tripped this repo's `*BATCH*.md` gitignore rule (case-insensitive match on macOS), silently leaving it untracked by git despite being fully written. Force-added it; the pattern is broad enough to catch any future ADR titled with the word "batch."

### Fix: scheduled health check flagged a real leaked chain-of-thought fragment in Ciaran's package (ADR-0093) and a real 9-character gap on an unrelated month-old order
Two separate hits from the scheduled GitHub Actions health-check bot, both verified genuine (not false alarms) by running the exact detector queries directly rather than trusting the digest summary.

**Meta-text leak, Ciaran's package:** `list_packages_with_meta_text_leak()` flagged "Muerte En El Micrófono." Re-fired the character once more (mechanism unchanged from ADR-0093); verified clean.

**Roster-count mismatch, "The Cognitive Dissonance Incident: A Murder At The MSU Psychology Department Picnic":** 16 of 25 approved characters actually existed, purchased 2026-07-27. Unlike the backlog packages Jonathan already decided not to touch (all 4+ months old, "party already happened"), this one is inside the 30-day window — so remediating it is consistent with that decision, not an exception to it. ### Fix: chain-of-thought/prose leaks now self-heal via auto-remediation instead of always escalating to a human ([ADR-0099](docs/adr/0099-delegate-chain-of-thought-leaks-to-auto-remediation.md))
Jonathan asked why the meta-text leak above sat live for ~24 hours despite `auto-remediate-packages` running every 30 minutes. Traced it precisely: the worker DID run, DID detect it within 15 minutes (`auto_remediation_log` shows `template_artifact` / `escalate:no_mechanical_fix` logged 2026-08-20 12:43 UTC), and made a deliberate, documented choice not to attempt a fix — `stripArtifactLines()`'s own comment stated flatly that chain-of-thought "is never touched here... which is correct." Detection was never the gap; nothing acted on it.
- Root cause: `ARTIFACT_TOKEN_RX`/`ARTIFACT_SPAN_RX` only recognized 3 of the 13 phrases in the SQL detector's marker regex (`\[choose`, `\[closing paragraph`, `master_context`) — free-text phrases like "wait, i need to" and two bracket patterns (`\[insert `, `\[if guilty`) were invisible to the repair logic, so a field containing only one of them looked clean and the whole package fell through to an uninformative escalate.
- Extended `stripArtifactLines` to recognize the missing patterns and route prose-only leaks (no bracket to excise) straight to the same `delegateToRegenerator` → `regenerate-child-content` path already trusted for `identity_contamination`/`slip_culprit_leak` — same re-detect-and-revert safety net, same attempt cap, same spend cap, no new infrastructure.
- Verified via an isolated unit test of the pure function (10 cases including Sandra's actual leaked text — 10/10 pass, existing bracket-strip/embedded behavior unchanged) plus a live `dry_run` smoke test against production post-deploy (v10, zero errors).
- Confirmed with Jonathan first — this changes what a shared production remediation system is allowed to touch unattended.

## 2026-08-20

### Fix: "Remove a Character" batch stuck at 0/9 for hours; manually completed customer's purchase, found two real transform bugs ([ADR-0098](docs/adr/0098-remove-character-batch-stuck-invocation-and-manual-recovery.md))
Customer (Lyn DiFranco) paid $5 to remove 9 characters, emailed hours later still showing "0 of 9" and needing to send links same-day. Traced it: `adapt-mystery-apply`'s first invocation claimed row 0, then hung forever with no error and no chain-dispatch (chain-dispatch — the only thing that advances a batch — lives in the function's `finally` block, which a dead invocation never reaches).
- Added `AbortSignal.timeout(45s)` to the function's two Anthropic fetch calls on the theory an un-timeout'd network call was the stall; deployed it. The retry hung too (3+ min, past the 45s cap) — ruled out a leaked Postgres lock and a stale cached deploy, but the real cause of the hang is still unknown. This fix is deployed and is a real improvement regardless, but did not resolve this specific incident.
- Bypassed the edge function entirely: wrote a local script replicating its deterministic transform logic byte-for-byte and ran it directly against production (no chain-dispatch, no Anthropic call, no hang risk). First pass: 4/9 verified, 5/9 correctly rolled back (safely — the verify-or-revert gate caught the problem instead of leaving stale references).
- The 5 rollbacks exposed two real, previously-unknown bugs in the shipped transform, confirmed against live data: (1) `secrets` is a jsonb array-of-one-string, same real shape as `evidence_cards`, but the code only special-cases `evidence_cards` for that shape — every `secrets` mention of a removed character was silently skipped, not scrubbed; (2) the bare-surname regex fallback has no word-boundary, so a surname like "Cross" matches inside unrelated words ("across", confirmed live) — a false-positive verify failure, and a would-be garbled substitution if it fired during transform instead. Fixed both in the manual script only, re-ran the 5 failed rows — all verified clean.
- **Result: all 9 characters removed, all 9 `mystery_adaptations` rows `verified`, 0 references to any removed character remain anywhere in the package** — checked directly against the database, not inferred.
- **Not yet done — tracked in the ADR:** bugs 2 and 3 need porting into the deployed `adapt-mystery-apply/index.ts` and redeploying (low risk, already validated, deliberately not rushed into the same motion as the emergency fix). The original hang's root cause is still open — the next real purchase could hit the same stuck-batch experience.

### Fix: extended notify-generation-issue's auto-recovery to genuinely-missing character rows, not just empty ones ([ADR-0097](docs/adr/0097-missing-character-row-auto-recovery.md))
Jonathan received a stuck-generation alert mid-remediation on The Staged Suicide Details (13 of 15 characters) and asked whether manually checking with an AI agent every time is the intended workflow. Traced it: `emptyCharacters` only ever filtered EXISTING `mystery_characters` rows — a roster slot that was never inserted at all (as opposed to a row that exists but is incomplete, ADR-0096's shape) was invisible to every check and so never got offered to auto-recovery, meaning the alert fired immediately with no grace period, because nothing was going to fix it. This is the exact gap ADR-0094's Consequences section named and deferred.
- Extended the existing recovery loop (same `CHILD_WEBHOOK`, same 2-attempt cap, same shared spend cap) to also cover names present in `extracted_characters` with no matching row, logged under a distinct `defect_class: "missing_character_row"` for audit clarity, attempt cap now spans both defect classes.
- Widened the alert-suppression condition so missing-row recovery gets the same "don't page a human while recovery still has budget left" grace period the empty-row case already had — this is the actual fix to Jonathan's question: a missing-row alert will now only reach him if recovery genuinely can't fire or exhausts its cap.
- Deployed `notify-generation-issue` v25, `verify_jwt: true` preserved.

### Fix: rebuilt The Staged Suicide Details around the customer's actual 15-suspect concept, not the wrong 14-character cast from the previous day's fix
Customer (Lydia) replied to the ADR-0095 remediation email: "some characters were completely different, and some not even there... I made some people specifically for this mystery." Investigation confirmed she was right and it was worse than the roster-count bug: she'd designed a 27-player concept (12 investigator characters + 15 suspects, explicitly no accomplice) across the whole chat, but `conversations.player_count` was never updated from a stale 14, and her final reformatted roster got split across two messages by the AI's own response-length limit — `approved_concept_message_id` only ever pointed at the second half (7 names). That mismatch against the stale player_count triggered the Claude-fallback extraction path (ADR-0069), which pulled from a truncated context window and landed on 14 names, 5 of which (Sarah Chen, Marcus Webb, Officer Garrett, Diane Foster, Thomas Brecken) don't exist anywhere in her actual conversation — a hallucinated substitute cast.

The product's real, already-existing mechanism for this (per Jonathan) is extra guests playing as scriptless co-investigators alongside the suspects, not 12 additional generated characters.
- Sent Lydia a 3-option email (rebuild around the 15 real suspects with investigators as scriptless co-players; rebuild all 27 as suspects, which needs her help giving the 12 investigators personal murder motives; or a refund). She chose option 1.
- Rebuilt: reconstructed her true 15-suspect concept verbatim from the actual transcript, verified it parses to exactly 15 names via the real shipped extractor (esbuild-transpiled, not a hand copy) before touching the database, inserted it as a new message, deleted the wrong 14-character cast, corrected `player_count` to 27, reset the package's generation state, and re-triggered the full pipeline (`mystery-webhook-trigger` → Make.com parent + child). Landed at 13/15 on the first pass — the completion gate correctly held it at `needs_review` rather than shipping short (ADR-0094/0095/0096 working as designed) — manually re-fired the 2 missing characters (Miles Porman, Lexi Grahmn) via the same recovery webhook.

Customer emailed with a link to the rebuilt mystery.

### Fix: Ciaran's "fully remediated" package (ADR-0093) was actually only 11/24 characters fixed; auto-recovery never forwarded customer language at all
Ciaran emailed again: several character packs still had Spanish text. The 2026-08-19 "final sweep — 0 non-English" claim in ADR-0093's addendum only checked the `## CHARACTER DESCRIPTION` header field, not the actual round-script/secret content — and only 11 of Ciaran's 24 characters had ever been re-fired (8 missing + 2 known-Portuguese + Richie for the token bug). The other 13, from the original 2026-08-18 run, were never touched and were still substantially in Spanish or Portuguese — e.g. one character's `secret` field entirely in Portuguese while `round2_innocent` on the same row was entirely in Spanish.
- Built a full-content sweep using the template's own section headers translated into Spanish/Portuguese/French (`## RONDA 2`, `## SEU SEGREDO`, `**SI ERES**`) rather than accented characters alone — the accent-only heuristic threw false positives on a year of legitimate French/Spanish-themed flavor text. Ran across every paid customer, not just Ciaran's: found exactly one other hit, a legitimate all-French mystery (customer's own concept was in French) — **confirmed this incident is contained to Ciaran's package, not systemic**.
- Re-fired the 13 untouched characters via the child scenario's webhook (same mechanism as ADR-0089/0093), this time adding `"language": "English"` to the payload by hand — the payload shape these remediations have always copied never included a `language` field, so without adding it explicitly, none of the 13 would have gotten the fix they needed. One (Chantelle/Charlie Frost) silently no-showed on first fire (HTTP 200, no DB write); one isolated retry fixed it.
- **Result after a second retry round: 21 of 24 characters fully clean English.** 3 have a reproducible residual defect, confirmed on 2 consecutive independent re-fires each: Deano/Deanna Harper and Maureen/Maurice Briggs both fail identically on accomplice-slip only; Tracey/Travis Bennett fails identically on innocent-slip AND guilty-slip. Tommo/Tamsin Clarke is a different failure mode — 3 separate webhook fires all returned HTTP 200 but never wrote to the DB at all.
- **Also fixed**: `notify-generation-issue/index.ts` — the auto-recovery function that fires every 10 minutes for any package stuck in `needs_review` — never sent a `language` field on its own re-fire calls to the same child webhook, independent of and predating this incident. Added the same `LANGUAGE_NAMES`/`profiles.language` lookup as `mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts`. Without this, the *automated* recovery path would keep silently reproducing this whole defect class for any future customer, even once the Make.com-side fix is fully reliable. Deployed to production (`notify-generation-issue` v24, `verify_jwt: true` preserved).
- Full trail in [ADR-0093](docs/adr/0093-explicit-language-parameter-for-child-generation.md)'s Addendum 3.

### Fix (addendum): found why the "explicit language" fix hasn't actually worked since it shipped — for anyone, not just Ciaran
`MAKE_API_TOKEN` in `.env` turned out to be usable (already known per ADR-0095/0096, missed before writing the entry above). Pulled both live scenarios' blueprints directly via the Make API and found the real root cause: `mystery-webhook-trigger` and both scenarios' Claude prompts all correctly handle `language`, but **neither the Parent nor the Child scenario's webhook trigger module (`gateway:CustomWebHook`, id `63` in both) has `language` in its declared data-structure interface** — Make silently drops any incoming field that isn't in that list before the scenario runs. `{{63.language}}` has been resolving to an empty string on every character generation since `Parent55`/`Child33` went live on 2026-08-19, for every customer, not just Ciaran's leftovers — explains the scattered residual-failure pattern above (a uniformly blank language directive, not a broken module, with failure rate tracking how much foreign-flavor text sits in each call's own context).
- Fix drafted, not yet imported: added `language` (type `text`) to both webhook interfaces. Built as `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)36-WebhookLanguageField.blueprint.json` (from `Child35`) and `temp-files/MM Live - Parent56 (Webhook Language Field).blueprint.json` (from `Parent55`). Diffed clean against the live-pulled originals — exactly the one interface field plus each blueprint's `name` changed.
- Did not push live via the API — this changes the production generation path for every customer; left as a drafted file for Jonathan to import, per this codebase's established workflow.
- **Until this imports, it is not accurate to tell any customer their language issue is "fully sorted"** — the underlying mechanism has been non-functional in production this whole time, for any mystery whose setting leans into non-English flavor text.

### Fix: two live paid packages shipped with missing characters and empty round content; closed both gaps that let it happen ([ADR-0095](docs/adr/0095-bracketless-extracted-characters-third-parse-shape.md), [ADR-0096](docs/adr/0096-missing-round-content-blocking-defect.md))
Flagged by the scheduled GitHub Actions health-check bot (ADR-0064's roster-mismatch detector): The Staged Suicide Details [approved=7, actual=10] and The Birthday Betrayal [approved=10, actual=9]. Both purchased 2026-08-19, both hours *after* the previous day's ADR-0094 fix shipped.

**Bug 1 — bracketless `extracted_characters` (ADR-0095):** `package_expected_character_count()` (ADR-0094) handled two shapes of `extracted_characters` — a real JSON array, or a JSON string that's already a valid array once unquoted — but not a third, live shape: a bare comma-joined sequence of JSON objects with no enclosing `[ ]` at all. Both packages hit this exact shape, so the row-count guard never activated. Staged Suicide Details was missing 4 of 14 characters, including the predetermined killer (host-facing `detective_script` still correctly named him — generated from the complete original `master_context`, unaffected). Birthday Betrayal was missing 1 of 10, referenced by name in three other characters' `relationships` text.
- Fixed `package_expected_character_count()` with a second parse attempt (wrap in `[ ]`, retry) before falling back to 0.
- Manually remediated both packages: re-fired the 5 missing characters via the same `CHILD_WEBHOOK` `notify-generation-issue` already uses for auto-recovery (2 needed a second attempt).
- **Follow-up sweep after applying**: 4 more hits. "Whispers From The Void" (known, intentional). "Death In The Spotlight" (unpaid, matches a known false-signal timestamp — not live). "Hearts In Hot Water" and "Blood In The Bougainvillea" (both real paid orders, several months old) flagged separately, not remediated in this pass — see ADR-0095 Consequences.

**Bug 2 — missing round content, no detector anywhere (ADR-0096):** independently, one character per package (Han Yu, Casey/Cassidy Chen) had fully populated identity fields but all 7 round-script/final-statement fields empty. Investigated the token-budget theory from ADR-0093 first and ruled it out — checked the *live* Make.com scenario via its API and confirmed module 409 already runs at `max_tokens: 6000` (ADR-0093's fix is genuinely live, despite this file's own stale "not yet imported" note above — corrected). Execution logs show `status: success` for the relevant runs; not a crash, a silent content drop with no visibility at this session's API access level. Reading `package_completion_blocking_defects()` directly found the real gap: it checks 8 other defect classes but never round-script/final-statement completeness, and neither does any async detector.
- Fixed both characters via `regenerate-child-content` (fields whitelisted, accept-or-revert gate; Han Yu needed one retry after the re-detect gate rejected the first attempt).
- Added a `missing_round_content` defect class to `package_completion_blocking_defects()` — the one function already wired into all three completion gates — and widened `notify-generation-issue`'s existing auto-recovery detection to match, so future occurrences self-heal via the existing capped re-fire mechanism with zero new machinery.
- **Historical sweep**: 21 packages / ~100 characters match, all real paid orders, all dated before the 2026-08-11 token-budget fix and none after — consistent with a pre-fix backlog never backfilled, not an ongoing pattern. Flagged separately, not remediated in this pass — real decision on scope/cost/customer communication needed first.
- **Found an orphaned prior fix**: `get_empty_characters()` (migration `20260422125154`, four months old) already implements almost this exact check — but was never wired into any caller anywhere in the codebase or database. It shipped the same day as two of the worst-hit historical packages, ~5 hours before them. Left in place unused; not reused (different design, and the shared-function pattern this fix follows is more consistent with ADR-0049's precedent).

## 2026-08-19

### Fix: packages could silently ship "completed" while missing whole characters ([ADR-0094](docs/adr/0094-recovery-path-character-count-gate.md))
Follow-up to the Ciaran Fox incident above (ADR-0093), which deliberately deferred this exact gap: `generation_status` could report `completed` even when `mystery_characters` has fewer rows than the customer's approved roster. Traced the live DB functions directly (not the migration files) and found the mechanism: `validate_package_characters()` (the trigger firing once on `generation_completed_at` going `NULL -> NOT NULL`) already correctly holds a package at `needs_review` when characters are missing — but the two recovery paths that promote `needs_review -> completed` every 2 minutes via `pg_cron` (`heal_completed_packages()`, `promote_complete_packages()`) only check that *existing* character rows aren't empty — neither re-derives the expected roster size. A package correctly held for 8 missing characters, with its 16 existing rows all well-formed, satisfied every check those two functions had and got silently re-promoted on the very next cron tick. This is almost certainly what happened to Ciaran's package.
- Extracted the roster-size parser that was inline inside `validate_package_characters()` into a new shared function, `package_expected_character_count()`, and added a row-count guard to `heal_completed_packages()` and `promote_complete_packages()` — same pattern ADR-0049 already used to close the structural-defect version of this gap.
- Deliberately sourced from `mystery_packages.extracted_characters` (the roster parsed from the approved chat concept), **not** `conversations.player_count` — player_count is guest headcount, which the product intentionally allows to exceed character count (extra guests co-investigate rather than getting their own character, ADR-0064's Discussion). Using player_count as a hard floor would have false-positived on every such package.
- **Historical sweep**: compared character count against `player_count` for every `completed` package. 21 came back short; investigated each. 1 is the already-known, intentional "Whispers From The Void" guest-dropout case. The other 20 all trace to pre-ADR-0043 (2026-07-26) legacy rows already investigated and closed in the 2026-08-13 CHANGELOG entry, with `updated_at` bumped by the 2026-08-01 JSON-normalization migrations, not by any recent activity. No other live instance of this bug found. Zero packages currently sit in `needs_review`, so the migration shipped against a clean slate.
- **Verified** in a rolled-back transaction against synthetic test rows: a package short 2 of 4 expected characters (both existing rows well-formed) correctly stayed `needs_review` after both cron functions ran; a complete 4-of-4 package still promoted normally (positive control, no regression).
- **Not addressed**: why characters fail to generate in the first place (Make.com parent/child ack-blindness, already traced in ADR-0093) and auto-recovery for entirely-missing character rows (existing auto-recovery only handles rows that exist but are empty) — both remain manual/separate follow-ups. This fix only guarantees the false "completed" signal can't happen; the existing 10-minute alert sweep + 6-hour cooldown still has to page a human for the rest.
- `supabase/migrations/20260819_close_recovery_path_character_count_gap.sql` — applied directly to production.

### Fix: character-generation prompt could drift into the wrong language despite an English-language order ([ADR-0093](docs/adr/0093-explicit-language-parameter-for-child-generation.md))
Customer Ciaran Fox reported his paid 24-character package generated only 16 characters and had content in an unexpected language. Confirmed both live: 2 of 16 generated characters came back entirely in Portuguese despite `profiles.language = 'en'` and clean English input, traced to the Child (Unified) scenario's Claude prompt asking the model to *detect* output language from `master_context`/`conversationContent` on every call instead of being told explicitly — unreliable specifically because this mystery's English concept was rich with Spanish setting/flavor text (Bar Estrella, Costa del Sol, sangria), which some of the ~8 per-character Claude calls misread as the target language.
- `mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts`: added a `LANGUAGE_NAMES` map, fetches `profiles.language`, forwards it as `language` in the webhook payload sent to Make.com — this field never existed in the payload before.
- Built `temp-files/MM Live - Parent55 (Explicit Language Parameter).blueprint.json` (adds `"language": "{{63.language}}"` to all 8 modules that send a character to the Child scenario) and `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)33-ExplicitLanguageParameter.blueprint.json` (all 8 Claude prompt modules now say `Write ALL output in {{63.language}}` instead of "detect the language," plus an explicit warning not to drift based on in-story foreign flavor text).
- **Not yet imported into Make.com** — drafted this session, no Make.com API access; Jonathan needs to import both blueprints live (parent + child together, so `{{63.language}}` doesn't resolve empty) and verify before publishing.
- **Not addressed by this fix**: why 8 of the 24 characters never got a `mystery_characters` row inserted at all (separate, still-open investigation — see vault note), and the underlying gap that `generation_status` can report `completed` with fewer character rows than `player_count` with nothing catching it.
