### Fix (addendum): Ciaran's package remediated + a 3rd distinct generation bug found and fixed
`Parent55`/`Child33` (above) imported into Make.com. Verified with one real re-fire (Jody/Jordan Matthews) before the full remediation — came back clean English. Then fired the remaining 8 missing characters + the second Portuguese character (Kayleigh/Kyle Brooks) directly via the child scenario's webhook (same recovery mechanism as ADR-0089). Result: all 24 characters present, zero language errors across the board.
- **New bug found during verification**: Richie/Regina "The Wolf" Castellano consistently came back with 7 fields empty (all "innocent-slip" content: `round2/3/4_questions`, `round2/3/4_innocent`, `final_innocent`) on both the original run and a re-fire — same failure both times, not random. Root cause: the Claude call producing those 7 fields (module `509`) has `max_tokens: 4000`, while its sibling calls producing *fewer* fields (`513`: 4 fields, `517`: 5 fields) get `max_tokens: 5000` — backwards budget allocation. Richie's dense money-laundering backstory most likely pushed the 7-field response past 4000 tokens before the JSON closed, producing unparseable output that silently dropped everything from that call.
- Bumped module `509` to `max_tokens: 6000` — built as `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)34-InnocentSlipTokenBudget.blueprint.json`, imported and verified: Richie re-fired a third time, all 7 fields now populate correctly.
- **Final result**: Ciaran's package fully remediated. Sweep across all 24 characters — 0 non-English, 0 bad headers, 0 incomplete rows.
- **Audited all 8 Claude calls in the child scenario for the same token-budget pattern**: module `409` (detective route) is a structural twin of the call that just failed — same 7 fields, same paragraph density, plus it carries the murderer's full confession — sitting at the same undersized `4000` tokens, untested but very plausibly the same latent bug. Bumped to `6000`. Also bumped `401`/`501` (identity/intro, 6 fields/5 prose blocks each, run for every character in every mystery) to `5000` as cheap defensive headroom — lower confidence of an active bug there, but same failure class. Left `405`/`505` (short list fields, no prose) and `513`/`517` (already proportionate) unchanged. Built as `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)35-DetectiveAndIdentityTokenBudget.blueprint.json`. **Not yet imported/tested.**
- **Also fixed, separately**: the package title (`死亡en El Micrófono: Murder At The Costa Del Karaoke` — a stray Chinese character where the concept-chat model most likely meant the Spanish "Muerte") was untouched by any of the above, since it originates in the original chat message before Make.com is ever invoked. Fixed via SQL update on `mystery_packages.title` and `conversations.title`. Casing corrected in a follow-up pass to `Muerte En El Micrófono: Murder At The Costa Del Karaoke` after sampling other titles confirmed this product capitalizes every word regardless of length. Confirmed via the actual chat transcript that the customer never discussed or specified a title at all — only theme, setting, tone, player count, and mechanics — so this restoration doesn't override anything he explicitly asked for.
- **Checked whether the stray Chinese character needs a systemic fix — concluded no.** `mystery-ai/index.ts` (the concept-chat generator) already uses explicit client-selected language plus a strong directive, not detection-from-content — the same design just retrofitted into the Make.com child scenario above. Scanned all 137 other package titles for non-CJK-locale customers: zero other occurrences. Genuine one-off; existing safeguard is working as designed.
- Full trail in [ADR-0093](docs/adr/0093-explicit-language-parameter-for-child-generation.md)'s addendum.

### Fix: abandoned "Remove a Character" checkout permanently blocked retries + showed a false "in progress" UI ([ADR-0092](docs/adr/0092-adaptation-checkout-abandonment-reconciliation.md))
Found live-testing the flow: went through Stripe Checkout, closed the browser without paying, came back to the mystery and saw a permanent "Update in progress" spinner at 0% for work that was never happening. Root cause: `mystery_adaptations` rows are created `'pending'` before the Stripe redirect, and nothing ever moved them out of `'pending'` for an abandoned checkout — `checkout.session.expired` was subscribed on the live webhook but its handler was a no-op, and even fixed, Stripe's default 24h session expiry meant up to a full day locked out. Worse: `adapt-mystery-create`'s "only one batch in flight per package" guard treats a stuck `'pending'` row as still in flight, so the package couldn't start a new removal request at all until this shipped.
- `stripe-webhook/index.ts`: `checkout.session.expired` now releases `adaptation-batch:` rows to `status: 'failed', error_message: 'checkout_expired'`, mirroring the existing `completed` handler's idempotent update pattern.
- `adapt-mystery-create/index.ts`: Checkout Session `expires_at` shortened from Stripe's 24h default to 60 minutes — balances not rushing a real customer against not leaving a "guest just cancelled" emergency tool locked out for most of a day.
- Manually unblocked the two rows stuck from this test (package `ffea7320-ba7e-48a3-a5c2-9fcf2ba8112a`) after confirming via the Stripe API that the session was genuinely never paid — verified zero remaining non-terminal rows for that package afterward.
- Deployed: `stripe-webhook` v66, `adapt-mystery-create` v4, `send-adaptation-complete-email` v4 (bundled the ADR-0091 rename fix for that email's header, found while in this code). `adapt-mystery-apply`'s equivalent rename (header comment only) is committed locally but not redeployed — not worth the transcription risk of manually redeploying 1,315 lines for a comment change.
- **Not verified**: an actual live 60-minute abandoned-checkout → `expired`-webhook round trip — would need either a real hour-long wait or Stripe CLI event-trigger tooling, neither available this session. The code path mirrors the already-proven `completed` handler closely.
- **Not addressed**: the explicit-Cancel path (clicking Cancel on Stripe's page) still takes up to 60 minutes to release rather than instantly — no dedicated cancel-and-release endpoint built. Follow-up if this shows up in real support volume.

### Fix: Child scenario generates all character content in English regardless of customer language — Make.com prompt fix drafted, not yet imported
Investigating our first real foreign-language customer (`profiles.language = 'pt'`, package `57acfc47-9051-4f60-853e-ebec850d2127`, "Morte No Topo: O Último Brinde De Vivienne") to determine scope before starting the broader Host Guide/Character Guide localization work. But every `mystery_characters` field (Child scenario output — `background`, `introduction`, `round2_script` through `round4_script`, `final_statement`, etc.) came back 100% in English, including literal English section headers baked into the prose itself (`"## CHARACTER BACKGROUND"`, `"Read this aloud when introducing yourself"`).

This didn't matter for the Parent scenario because all 10+ of its Claude modules wrap their prompts in a `<language_instruction>` block that infers language directly from the conversation/`master_context` text (e.g. `"Always respond in the same language as the master_context provided below"`). The Child scenario's 8 Claude modules (character background/relationships/secret/introduction, rumors/accusations, round 2-4 scripts, final statement/reveal) have **no such instruction at all**, and their `output_schema` templates hardcode English markdown headers and bold labels for the model to reproduce verbatim — so even with no language signal, the embedded headers would still come out English.

### Fix: customer's package had 0/6 characters despite `generation_status: completed` — two Make.com Child scenario bugs, both fixed live
Customer `annrelli@aol.com` ("The Jealous Niece") purchased and generation reported `completed`, but `mystery_characters` had zero rows — the "We're Finalizing" screen never cleared, and `notify-generation-issue`'s own empty-character auto-recovery is a no-op when there are no existing rows to iterate over, so this needed manual escalation. Root-caused live against the customer's actual Make.com execution log, not just the checked-in blueprint. Full writeup: [ADR-0089](docs/adr/0089-child-scenario-id-chaining-and-filter-operator-regression.md).
- **Bug 1**: the "Identity Parsed OK" filter (added in ADR-0087) had its comparator operator blank/unset live in both routes (detective 404, character 504), so the identity write was skipped every time regardless of whether Claude's output was valid — confirmed via a direct pull of the module's output showing clean, complete JSON being blocked anyway. Fixed live in Make's UI (set to "Exists", writes `"o": "exist"` — not the `"text:exist"` value the checked-in blueprint had, which may not be a value Make's import path honors for this filter type).
- **Bug 2**: ADR-0087 had deliberately repointed 6 downstream `upsertARecord` modules (408/412, 508/512/516/520) from chaining off the prior upsert's own id (`{{404.id}}`/`{{504.id}}`, the pattern used from Child14 through Child27) to the one-time `searchRows` result (`{{400.id}}`/`{{500.id}}`) — reasoned protection against a case where the new filter skips 404/504. That result is empty not just when skipped, but on *every* first-time single-pass character generation, so every write after the first hit `mystery_characters_package_character_unique` (409, silently queued to Incomplete Executions). Restored the pre-ADR-0087 chaining; the narrow case ADR-0087 was protecting against is reopened as a known, documented gap (see ADR-0089's Alternatives Considered for the `COALESCE` fix that would close both cases at once — not implemented yet).
- **Recovered this customer's package manually**: re-fired all 6 characters via the child webhook directly, verified full field completion (identity, rumors/accusations, all round 2-4 branches, final innocent/guilty) for all 6, confirmed exactly 6 rows. ~10 individual character-webhook fires across iterative debugging, approved in advance with a cost estimate.
- **Backfilled `character_role`** from the `invalid_role` sentinel to `suspect` for all 6 rows (free, deterministic — separate pre-existing bug where the model echoes the prompt's parenthetical instruction text instead of just outputting `"suspect"`; not fixed at the prompt level, only backfilled for this customer).
- **Not done — flagged as follow-up**: no sweep run yet to check whether other customers hit the same 0-character failure in the window this bug was live (~2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16). Given the fix requires a genuinely first-time single-pass generation to manifest, likely rare but unconfirmed.
- **Fixed and re-exported**: `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)30-FixIdChaining.blueprint.json` matches the corrected live scenario.

### Improvement: Character Guide round headers now take priority over the AI's own embedded header
Owner noticed reading the Characters tab: the "what to do now" round-context note (e.g. "Round 1 — Rumors, right after introductions") rendered as a small, muted blockquote *before* the section, while a separate, larger, more generic heading (either the AI's own embedded `## RUMORS TO SPREAD`-style header, or a fallback like "Rumors") rendered *after* it — backwards visual priority, with two competing headings for one section. Confirmed via Supabase: 96% of `introduction`/`rumors` fields carry their own embedded markdown header, so this wasn't rare.
- **`src/components/EditableSection.tsx`**: added an optional `hideHeader` prop that suppresses only the *visible* header row — the internal extraction/stripping and save-reconstruction logic is untouched, so editing and saving a field still preserves its original embedded header in the database. No DB writes are affected by this change.
- **`src/components/MysteryPackageTabView.tsx`**: split the round-labeled entries out of `ROUND_INTENT` into a new `ROUND_HEADERS` map (`{title, instruction}`) covering Introduction, Rumors, Round 2–4, Accusations, Final Statements, and The Reveal confessions. These now render as an actual `<h3>` title (e.g. "Round 2 — Motives") with the "what to do now" instruction directly below it in italic, and pass `hideHeader` to `EditableSection` so the AI's own embedded header doesn't render a second, competing heading underneath. `character_name`'s non-round editing tip stays on the old `ROUND_INTENT` blockquote path, unaffected.
- Static template (like the Host Guide), so retroactive for every past and future customer automatically — nothing to backfill.
- **Verification gap, flagged not hidden**: the interactive Characters tab with edit controls only renders on the authenticated `/mystery/:id` route; the no-login `/host/:token` route (`HostAccess.tsx`) has its own separate rendering untouched by this change. No login session available this session to get an actual screenshot. Verified: clean typecheck, no new lint errors, and the new heading reuses `EditableSection`'s own exact className pattern (not a guessed match). Not verified: an actual rendered screenshot.

### Fix: character occasionally listed as its own ally/rival ("You are yourself")
Owner spotted "Celeste/Cecil Fontaine — You are yourself" under Allies/Rivals on a live package. Queried `mystery_characters.relationships` for exact matches: 5 rows across 3 packages (2026-07-03 to 2026-08-02), every one a dual-gender-variant name (e.g. "Celeste/Cecil Fontaine", "Evangeline/Evander Blackwood") — rare, not the norm, but a real reproducing bug, not a one-off fluke. Root cause in `supabase/functions/regenerate-child-content/index.ts`: the "Full cast" roster sent to the relationship-generation prompt was built from *all* characters in the package with no exclusion of the character being written about, so the model could (and did) pick itself off that list as an ally/rival. Fixed by moving the cast-roster build inside the per-character loop and filtering out `character.id`.
- **Still open**: this function's `buildPrompt` comment says it "mirrors the Child blueprint's `<context>` block" — the original Make.com child scenario used for first-time generation likely has the same unfiltered-cast pattern and needs the equivalent fix at the source. Not done here (Make.com blueprint, out of this repo) — flagged as a vault note.
- No backfill of the 5 known-affected rows performed — low volume, deferred.

### Fix: italicized inconsistent `[Present Round X Evidence]` cues across full history
Separate bug from the earlier "Read after the Round X evidence card is revealed" contradiction (already fully backfilled) — this one is pure formatting inconsistency, not a factual error. Every other bracketed stage direction in `detective_script` is italicized (`*[...]*`); the `[Present Round X Evidence]` cue itself was split roughly 1:4 between italic and plain across the population (13 italic vs. 54 plain, 0 packages mixing both styles internally). Backfilled all 54 with a non-AI `regexp_replace` — `(?<!\*)\[(Present Round \d Evidence[^\]]*)\]` → `*[\1]*` — handles both the plain `[Present Round 2 Evidence]` form and the extended-description form (`[Present Round 2 Evidence: A leather-bound ledger...]`). Verified against the full table with no date filter: 0 non-italic instances remain anywhere.
- **Round 1 → transition note deliberately NOT backfilled.** Same investigation surfaced that 0/72 packages older than 30 days have any "move straight to Round 1" note after the Opening Statement, vs. 25/33 (76%) in the last 30 days — looks like a recent, partial Make.com prompt change rather than something that was ever fully rolled out. Checked whether historical packages have a reliable insertion point (the `---` + `## ROUND 1` header pattern): only 30 of the 81 missing packages match it cleanly; the other 51 use varied older formats (different heading levels, no separator, one an entirely different template). Unlike the evidence-cue fix, this is inserting new text rather than correcting existing text — with an unreliable anchor point across most of the population, auto-inserting risks malformed output. Deferred to a forward-only Make.com prompt fix; historical packages left as-is.
- **Make.com prompt corrections for both, still not applied at the source** (no scenario access from this session):
  - End of Opening Statement: add `*[Proceed immediately into Round 1 — there is no break here.]*`
  - Evidence-reveal cue: ensure the model always wraps it as `*[Present Round X Evidence]*` (or with a trailing description, `*[Present Round X Evidence: ...]*`), never unitalicized.

### Fix: "Running the Game" steps were rendering as run-on sentences
Owner caught it immediately on read-through: steps 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 read as one jumbled sentence — e.g. "Opening Statement — 2–3 min Deliver the Detective's Opening Statement: read it aloud..." — title and body smashed together with no visual break. Root cause: a single newline inside a markdown list item collapses to a space in the rendered output, not a line break; only the steps that happened to already contain a bullet list or a bold mid-sentence phrase (2, 4, 5) got a break "for free." Fixed by adding an actual blank line between each step's title and its body paragraph, which is real CommonMark syntax for multiple paragraphs inside one list item (needs matching indentation on the continuation line, not just a blank line).
- **Verified with the same real-pipeline method as the underlying redesign** — not eyeballed. Built a second test sample (detective-style, since it hadn't been checked before), parsed it through the app's actual `remark-parse`/`remark-gfm`, and confirmed every step now produces 2+ separate paragraph blocks (title, then body) instead of 1 merged block.
- Also dropped the odd "— 0 min" time badge on detective-style's "already set" step (not a timed action) in favor of "no action needed here."

### Improvement: Host Guide redesigned around one continuous "Running the Game" runbook
Follow-up to today's earlier round-flow fix (below) — that patch corrected wrong information, but a first-principles look (prompted by comparing against a competitor's host guide's simplicity) found the deeper problem: how the party actually runs was scattered across four non-adjacent sections (Quick-Start Checklist's round list, Time Guidelines, Determining the Culprit, Round-by-Round Flow), each describing it slightly differently. A host had to stitch four sections together to answer "what do I do first, second, third." `src/components/HostGuideTemplate.tsx` — static template, retroactive for every past and future customer, no backfill.
- **Collapsed Time Guidelines + Determining the Culprit + Round-by-Round Flow into one "Running the Game" section**, a strict numbered walkthrough (Opening Statement → Round 1 Part A: Introductions → Round 1 Part B: Rumors → Slip Draw *(character-based only)* → Round 2 → Round 3 → Round 4 → Accusations → Final Statements → The Reveal) with time estimates folded inline per step instead of a separately-repeated list. Detective-style mysteries get a one-line "already set, skip to Round 2" note in the same numbered slot rather than a separate section elsewhere in the doc.
- **Detective-style skip note moved to the top of the slip-draw step**, not buried as a trailing caveat — a detective-style host shouldn't have to read the whole character-based procedure to learn it doesn't apply to them.
- **Introduction pacing now computed from real player count** instead of a flat "20–25 min" that silently broke down for large groups. New `introMinutes()` helper (~45 sec/player, same pattern as the existing `timeGuidelines()`) renders as "~6 min for your group of 8" etc., live per mystery, plus an explicit large-group callout (15+ guests: keep it to 2–3 sentences, or 30 guests at 1 min each burns 30 minutes on introductions alone).
- **Found and fixed a second, related bug while rewriting the file**: "Materials" and "Preparation Before the Party" listed slip-draw supplies (container, slips, the cut-N-slips prep step) as universal items regardless of mystery style — detective-style hosts (predetermined culprit, no slip draw at all) were being told to prepare a draw they'd never use, directly contradicting the "no slip draw needed" note elsewhere in the same document. Both now correctly condition on `isCharacterBased`.
- Kept the "fair-play rule" callout (murderer may mislead but can't invent fresh lies under direct questioning) at its existing trigger point — right before Round 2, where the text instructs the host to announce it. It's not decorative: it came from real host feedback (commit `162935d`, 2026-07-22) after a live game where the murderer went off-script under direct questioning and broke the mystery's solvability.
- **Verified rendering, not just written**: built a real sample of the new template output and parsed it through the app's actual `remark-parse`/`remark-gfm` pipeline (not a visual guess) to confirm the two numbered lists (1–4, then 5–10, split correctly by the fair-play paragraph in between) render with correct sequential numbers and that step 10's body text stays grouped under its list item rather than breaking into a stray paragraph — markdown ordered-list continuation lines need indentation matching the marker width (3 spaces for "1.", 4 for "10."), which the first draft got wrong for the double-digit step.
- Reference used for structural inspiration only (not copied — competitor's paid product): the same "Masters of Mystery" host guide from earlier today, whose "Lead the Game" section is one continuous chronological walkthrough rather than mechanics split across several sections.

### Fix: Host Guide round-flow gaps and terminology mismatch vs. the actual Detective Script/character guide
Reviewing the Host Guide against a real generated Detective Script and character guide (`detective_script`, `mystery_characters.rumors`) surfaced two real discrepancies in `src/components/HostGuideTemplate.tsx` — a static template, so this fix is automatically retroactive for every past and future customer with no backfill needed:
- **Rumors was missing entirely** from "Round order at a glance" and "Round-by-Round Flow," even though every generated Detective Script combines it with Round 1 under a single `## ROUND 1: INTRODUCTIONS & RUMORS` header (confirmed across multiple live packages) — the two happen back-to-back with no break, not as separate sequential rounds. Added Rumors to both sections and to the character-based "Determining the Culprit" walkthrough ("After Round 1 introductions" → "After Round 1 (introductions and rumors)").
- **Round 3 was labeled "Means" in two places** (round-order line, time guidelines) while the Detective Script, the character-guide `ROUND_INTENT` helper text, and every other reference to it consistently say "Method." Normalized to "Method" everywhere in this file.
- **Evidence-reveal timing was described backwards.** The old flow said "1. Detective's opening delivered → 2. Reveal evidence → 3. Players ask questions," implying evidence comes right after the opening and before any narration. Querying real `detective_script` rows showed evidence is actually revealed *mid-script*, cued by a bracketed `[Present Round X Evidence]` marker partway through the Detective's narration — and in ~78% of packages generated in the last 60 days (32/41), the script's own round-header stage direction ("*Read after the Round X evidence card is revealed*") directly contradicts that mid-script cue, since it can't be true that the card is already shown before text that later tells you to present it. Rewrote the host guide's instructions to match the actual mechanic (evidence revealed mid-narration at the bracketed cue) rather than the wrong two-step framing.
- **Backfilled the 32 affected packages** (Supabase `mystery_packages.detective_script`, non-AI `regexp_replace`, scoped to `is_paid = true AND purchase_date > now() - 60 days`): swapped the contradictory `*[Read after the Round X evidence card is revealed.]*` for `*[Present the evidence when cued below — don't reveal it before this point.]*` wherever the literal string matched (32/41 rows in the window; the other 9 already had the AI's own non-contradictory stage direction and were left untouched). Verified 0 remaining matches post-update. Pure text substitution — no narrative content touched, no regeneration, no Anthropic spend.
- **Still open**: the Make.com generation prompt itself (out of this repo) needs the same correction applied at the source so future packages stop reproducing the contradiction, and the "predictable boilerplate" (NOTE FOR HOST / RECORDING GUIDELINES wrapper, near-identical across every package checked) is a candidate for hardcoding into a static template the way the Host Guide already is — flagged for an ADR, not built here.
- Also added the missing `rumors` entry to `ROUND_INTENT` in `MysteryPackageTabView.tsx` — every other round had a "what to do now" helper shown under it in the character guide; Rumors was the one gap.
- Reference used for structural inspiration only (not copied, it's a competitor's paid product): a "Masters of Mystery" host guide the owner had on hand, which separates Round 1 into Part A (Intros) and Part B (Rumours) — informed the decision to present Rumors as explicitly part of Round 1 rather than its own numbered round.

Recast/character removal (ADR-0088) went live 2026-08-15, but the 33 people who bought in the 30 days before that never saw it. Drafted and locked in a one-time backfill announcement, continuing the post-purchase pipeline work from ADR-0078/`docs/post-purchase-sequence-design.md`.

## 2026-08-15

### Fix: name/background mismatch in "The Host Herself" (Harper Blackwell / Harper Chen)
Scheduled health check (check 11, ADR-0048 `name_background_mismatch` sub-check) flagged its first-ever live positive: a paid package (delivered 2026-08-07) where the roster listed a character as **Harper Blackwell** but her own background, her own read-aloud introduction, and 5 of the other 11 characters' rumor sheets all named her **Harper Chen** — a genuine surname bleed, not the Jordan/Jordana gender-flexible naming convention the detector was tuned to ignore.
- Verified scope in Supabase before touching anything: contamination was confined to `background`, `introduction` (1 row) and `rumors` (5 rows) — exactly one clean occurrence of "Harper Chen" per field, nothing in round scripts, accusations, secrets, final statements, host guide, or evidence cards.
- Applied a targeted `REPLACE()` fix (not regeneration) across the 6 affected rows/7 fields, aligning the prose to the roster name "Harper Blackwell" since that's what the app displays and it was the only name never contradicted anywhere else in the package. Chose this over regeneration because the package has been in the customer's hands for 8 days — a full regenerate would swap out content they may already be using, and per ADR-0048 this class of defect is escalate-only precisely because it needs a human judgment call, not because it needs new content invented.
- Verified post-fix: zero remaining "Harper Chen" occurrences, "Harper Blackwell" now consistent everywhere she's referenced.

### Feature: "Recast" — production keys wired, evidence-plausibility prompt fix, owner purchase notification
Third pass today, ahead of flipping the feature live. Two follow-ups plus the actual production configuration.
- **Production Anthropic key set** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), scoped to this specific use, confirmed registered. `ENABLE_GUEST_DROPOUT_ADAPTATION` flipped to `true` in production — backend no longer 404s, but still unreachable by real users (frontend flag + rebuild not done yet, tracked separately).
- **Reassignment prompt fix for the evidence-card mismatch found earlier today**: `buildReassignPrompt`'s hard_rules now explicitly instruct the model to check whether an evidence item's *fixed, unchangeable physical description* can plausibly support the new SIGNIFICANCE explanation before rewriting it (a financial ledger can plausibly reveal a bribe or paper trail, but not a physical struggle; a torn photograph can place someone at a scene, but not prove a financial motive) — if no genuine connection exists, the model is told to keep the significance general rather than force an implausible link. Deployed to production (`adapt-mystery-apply`). Not re-verified with a fresh live test (the local scratch-stack key from earlier had expired) — relying on the existing verify/rollback safety net and mandatory host-review flag as the backstop, same as any other reassignment.
- **New owner purchase-notification email**, mirroring the existing party-purchase and Cold Case Files notification emails in `stripe-webhook`: fires at purchase time (not completion — `send-adaptation-complete-email` already covers that, to the customer), lists every character in the batch with role, flags any murderer/accomplice reassignment row for extra attention, links to the mystery. Fire-and-forgotten so it can never delay the customer's actual processing start. Exists specifically because the launch decision was to go live without further pre-launch testing — this is the feedback loop for catching problems after the fact.

### Feature: "Recast" — real Anthropic + Stripe verification, deployed to production (staging-only, flag off)
Follow-up to the build below: ran the feature against real infrastructure for the first time today, then deployed it to the real production Supabase project.
- **Real Sonnet 5 reassignment call ($0.40)**: removed a murderer, auto-selected a replacement from the remaining suspects, verified clean (zero leftover references anywhere). Output quality genuinely strong — the model built the new culprit's motive from their pre-existing secret rather than inventing something disconnected, and the confession read as specific and coherent. One real narrative seam surfaced by the design's mandatory host-review flag, not a mechanical failure: a murder-weapon evidence card was repurposed to imply a different kind of crime than it physically supports — exactly the class of issue that flag exists to catch.
- **Real Stripe test-mode checkout, end-to-end**: Checkout Session → completed payment (test card) → webhook received and signature-verified → row marked `paid` → chain-dispatch → `verified` ($0.05, plain removal). Installed the Stripe CLI for local webhook forwarding. `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` made env-configurable so a test-mode price can override the hardcoded live default without touching production behavior.
- **Deployed to the real production Supabase project**: 2 new migrations and 3 new edge functions (`adapt-mystery-create`, `adapt-mystery-apply`, `send-adaptation-complete-email`). Still fully dormant in production — `ENABLE_GUEST_DROPOUT_ADAPTATION` was never set there, and every new function 404s immediately without it.
- **Caught before it caused damage**: diffed `stripe-webhook` against its live production version before deploying this feature's new branch into it, and found production's live function (v61) contains a full "Cold Case Files" order-handling path (`handleColdCaseOrder`, buyer/owner emails, GA4 event) that doesn't exist anywhere in this repo's `main` branch — deployed directly to production at some point outside git. Deploying the local file as-is would have silently deleted live Cold Case order processing. Deployed a merge instead (live content as the base, only the new `adaptation-batch:` branch + `fireAndForget` helper added on top, v62), then backfilled the recovered Cold Case code into the local file so it stops being silently stale. Whether other deployed functions have similar undocumented drift from `main` is untracked — see vault note.

### Feature: "Recast" — multi-character removal + murderer/accomplice reassignment (ADR-0088, staging only)
Substantial rework of the guest-dropout adaptation feature (ADR-0036/0082), driven by owner review starting from a real anecdote: a guest cancelled 30 minutes before a party with no spare guest to hand their character to. Renamed the feature to "Recast" and rebuilt around three changes: multi-character batching (remove several people in one $5 submission, not one at a time), murderer/accomplice reassignment (previously blocked outright — now a different remaining character can take over that role), and loosened eligibility for character-style/slip-mechanic packages (any character is removable there — confirmed via `docs/generation-guardrails.md` G8 that nothing is guilt-specific in those games).
- **Multi-character batching**: `mystery_adaptations` rows now share a `batch_id`/`batch_sequence`, covered by one Stripe Checkout Session. Traced a real lost-update race if a batch's characters were processed concurrently (a blind read-modify-write on `conversations.player_count`; two removed characters both mentioned in a third character's `rumors` field could silently clobber each other's edit while both reported `'verified'`) — prevented via chain-dispatch (each removal, on completion, dispatches the next one itself, strictly sequential) plus a package-scoped concurrency claim mirroring `claim_package_for_remediation` exactly, protecting against two different batches racing the same package.
- **Murderer/accomplice reassignment**: a new, bounded Sonnet 5 call (structured outputs, same API shape as the existing polish pass) rewrites the promoted character's role, round scripts, and final statement, plus the detective script's reveal section and evidence cards' host-only significance notes — nothing else. Host picks the replacement or leaves it to "let us choose." Every reassignment is flagged for host review (no mechanical check can confirm "this reads as a convincing confession" the way the deterministic scrub's "zero leftover references" check can) — surfaced on the success page and in a new completion email, never silently marked as confidently verified as a plain removal.
- **Pricing corrected mid-build**: originally per-character, corrected to flat $5 per submission after walking through the actual (bounded) scope of a reassignment with the owner.
- **Non-blocking processing + new completion email**: a batch can take several minutes, longer with a reassignment. The real flow redirects to Stripe and back — processing happens on the post-payment landing page (`AdaptationSuccess.tsx`), not inside the picker dialog. That page now shows a live per-character checklist and an explicit "go to your mystery now" path instead of a trapped spinner; a new `send-adaptation-complete-email` function (English-only, modeled on `send-host-email`'s branding) covers hosts who close the tab.
- **Naming and tab framing**: "a guest can't make it" (a scenario description) renamed to "Recast" (a product name, covering both removal and reassignment), kept as supporting hook text. The Extras tab gained a section intro line and a muted "Coming soon" placeholder for the already-designed ADR-0078 hosting-tips video, so it reads as a growing catalog rather than one lonely card.
- **Design process**: a mock preview page (`/guest-dropout-preview`, zero backend, no env vars) was built and iterated through several rounds of live owner review — flat pricing, a genuinely invisible button (outline variant, dark-on-dark), a wall-of-text explainer reformatted to scannable point-form, repetitive per-character confirm-screen copy consolidated — before the real backend was built, so the UX shape was validated cheaply first.
- One research subagent encountered and correctly resisted a prompt-injection attempt (fabricated system-reminder-shaped tool output) during this session — no impact, recorded for the record.
- **Verified end-to-end against the local scratch Supabase stack**: regression (plain removal), multi-character batch with chain-dispatch (confirmed strictly sequential via timestamps, not concurrent), package-claim contention (reverts cleanly, no orphaned chain), mid-chain failure (a failed character still lets the rest of the batch complete), reassignment fail-closed behavior (no live Anthropic key in this environment — confirmed it fails cleanly with zero writes rather than silently succeeding), verify-failure rollback (byte-for-byte restore confirmed), and a full live Playwright walkthrough of the real UI (not just the mock preview) signed in as a local test user. **Caught and fixed one real bug in the process**: the new "exactly 1 murderer post-removal" check ran unconditionally and incorrectly rolled back valid character-style removals (those packages legitimately have zero murderers by design) — now scoped to detective-style packages only.
- Still staging-only, feature-flagged off in production. Full writeup, what's verified vs. not (real Stripe checkout and real reassignment output quality still need a live key), and the promote-to-prod checklist in [ADR-0088](docs/adr/0088-guest-dropout-multi-character-and-reassignment.md).

### Investigation: host_guide/timeline "null on 56% of packages" was a false alarm — real gap is 13 old pre-ADR-0043 records, zero live customer impact
Follow-up from yesterday's Alexandra Broadus refund: found `host_guide`/`timeline` null on 70 of 128 paid `completed` packages, escalating to 100% every month since May 2026. Traced it fully before treating it as urgent.
- **Not a regression.** `host_guide`/`timeline`/`preparation_instructions`/`hosting_tips` going null was the deliberate outcome of the 2026-04-25 "Static host guide template" refactor — that content moved from AI-generated-per-mystery to a static, parameterized component (`HostGuideTemplate.tsx`). Confirmed via the Make.com parent blueprint history (`temp-files/MM Live - Parent22` → `Parent23`, module 178's mapper dropped those three keys outright, and module 174's prompt was rewritten to explicitly tell Claude not to generate them) and the same-day CHANGELOG entry.
- **Live product is unaffected.** `MysteryPackageTabView.tsx:862` renders `HostGuideTemplate` whenever `gameOverview` is present (the normal case), and the PDF/print path is `window.print()` on that same live-rendered DOM (`print.css`) — not a separate export reading the empty columns. Customers were never actually served an incomplete host guide from this.
- **Real residual: 13 old records**, not 78 — checked each one. 1 is a test conversation. The other 12 were all created July-December 2025, well before the April 2026 migration; 7 of 12 have 0 characters at all, the rest have implausibly low character counts against their player counts — these are pre-`ADR-0043` instances of the "completed but empty" bug that fix (2026-07-26) was built to catch, just from before it existed. No `host_email` on any, `updated_at` clustered around a single 2026-07-02 batch touch, not ongoing activity. No action needed — already superseded by ADR-0043 for anything new.
- **Minor dead code identified, not yet cleaned up**: `mysteryPackageService.ts:327`'s status-repair check still references `host_guide` as a completeness signal (can never fire now that the column is permanently null by design), and `HostGuideTemplate.tsx` accepts a `hostingTips` prop that's passed in but never rendered anywhere. Low priority, cosmetic.

## 2026-08-14

### Fix: close the identity-field silent-blank-write gap — payload fix live, blueprint fix awaiting import (ADR-0087)
Investigated why Phoenix Rivers' `description`/`background`/`secret`/`relationships` never got touched across 2 re-fire attempts while round scripts wrote fine. Two-part finding: (1) the re-fire payload was missing `conversationContent`/`characterChatExcerpts` compared to the original full-generation call; (2) more likely the actual cause — the Child scenario's identity-field Claude call (module 401/501) has no error handling on its parse step, and `parse-claude-json` returns a 422 with no `data` key on a parse failure. Make doesn't halt the scenario on that 422, so the downstream upsert still fires, writing blank strings over whatever was there — confirmed round scripts are a fully independent call/write chain, explaining why they succeed regardless.
- **Shipped now**: added `conversationContent` (sourced from the already-persisted `mystery_packages.user_conversation`, same pattern `regenerate-child-content` already uses) to the re-fire payload. `characterChatExcerpts` deliberately not replicated — ADR-0054 already documented it as permanently unrecoverable, not worth duplicating that extraction logic in a second place. Deployed `notify-generation-issue` v19 → v20.
- **Built, not yet imported**: `Child (Unified)28-GuardIdentityParseFailure.blueprint.json` — adds a filter so the identity upsert only fires when the parse actually succeeded (skip-and-leave-recoverable, mirroring ADR-0052's coerce-not-reject precedent for `character_role`), and repoints 6 downstream modules' `id` references so skipping the identity upsert can't break round-script/rumor writes for the same character. JSON valid, module count unchanged, diff shows exactly the 8 intended changes. Needs Jonathan's manual Make.com import.
- Full record in [ADR-0087](docs/adr/0087-identity-field-silent-blank-write-on-parse-failure.md).

Added a support-page FAQ entry (`supportPage.faqs.questions.roundCount`, `en.json` + `faq1.tsx`) stating the same. English only for now — other 12 locales not yet translated.
- **Deferred, not done**: actually making round count configurable would require a structured UI field, forwarding it through `mystery-webhook-trigger`, and a conditional Make.com prompt/schema — real lift, not attempted here. Raised `DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` from 5.0 to 10.0 in both places it's hardcoded (kept in sync, one shared ceiling per ADR-0076): `notify-generation-issue` (v18→v19) and `auto-remediate-packages` (v6→v7).

### Feature: SEO/GEO effectiveness tracking — durable snapshot history + retroactive backfill (ADR-0084)

Follow-up to today's earlier SEO/GEO documentation audit: Jonathan asked whether we can tell if `docs/seo-geo-playbook.md`'s recommendations are actually working, retroactively or otherwise. Built the free, immediately-available half (SEO/GA4 signals; true AI-citation confirmation is out of scope, needs a paid tool — see ADR-0084).

- **New `seo_performance_snapshots` table** (migration `20260813_seo_performance_snapshots.sql`) — `scripts/fetchSeoWeeklySnapshot.mjs` computed a rich GSC/GA4/AI-referral snapshot every week already, but only ever wrote it to a gitignored local JSON file that gets overwritten on every run. It now also inserts into this table (additive, try/catch'd like every other section — can't break the digest), so future weeks build a real time series instead of vanishing after one email.
- **New `scripts/backfillSeoHistory.mjs`** — pulls historical GSC (site-wide + blog-only) and GA4 AI-referral-traffic windows before/after a known past content intervention, using the fact that GSC/GA4 both retain ~14-16 months of history at Google, and writes pre/post rows into the same table tagged `source='backfill'`.
- **First run: March 2026 GEO enrichment (58 EN posts, stats/citations added).** Result was NOT a clean read — flagging clearly rather than overstating it:
  - Blog-page GSC: clicks 58→25 (-56.9%), impressions 4563→2187 (-52.1%), avg position 10.3→7.8 (improved). Site-wide GA4 sessions grew +14.5% (523→599) in the same window, so the blog-specific drop isn't a site-wide ranking problem.
  - AI-referral sessions: 4→0.
  - **Confound found after the fact:** the chosen intervention date (2026-03-17, from the "Full SEO/GEO Pipeline Complete" CHANGELOG entry) sat inside an active crisis, not a clean shipped-and-stable moment — `docs/blog-content-pipeline-history-2026-03.md` shows a mass Finnish-content-corruption incident (~573/754 posts) discovered 2026-03-15 with recovery still in progress ("Full Recovery: New Approach (Excel-First)") on 2026-03-16-17, and Phase 4 translation work explicitly marked IN PROGRESS past that date. The "post" window (Mar 27-Apr 26) overlaps that recovery, not a settled post-enrichment state.
  - **Conclusion:** this first case study can't be used to judge whether the playbook's GEO-enrichment claim held — pick a cleaner, more isolated intervention next (e.g. ADR-0045/0046, both well after the site stabilized) for an actual read. The pipeline itself is verified working end-to-end (real data pulled, computed, persisted, confirmed via SQL).

### Docs: rescued two SEO/GEO "learnings" documents that only existed in gitignored `temp-files/` — ADR-0083 backfilled

Jonathan asked whether ongoing SEO/GEO work and learnings are being durably captured for reuse on future projects. Audit found the week-to-week engineering trail in good shape (ADR-0018, ADR-0045, ADR-0046 etc. + weekly digest archives in `docs/seo-digests/` are all tracked and vault-synced), but two documents meant to capture *transferable* learnings were sitting only in `temp-files/`, which `.gitignore` strips (`temp-files/**/*.md`) — never committed, never vault-synced, one `mv`/cleanup away from being lost entirely:

- **`temp-files/seo-geo-playbook.md`** — the general SEO/GEO strategy playbook (content-length targets, GEO citation tactics, competitive landscape, technical foundations) — promoted to [docs/seo-geo-playbook.md](docs/seo-geo-playbook.md).
- **`temp-files/SEO_GEO_CHANGELOG.md`** — a March 2026 history of the blog voice-rewrite/GEO-enrichment/translation pipeline, including an undocumented incident: a translation-propagation bug wrote Finnish content into ~573 of 754 published posts across languages (21 of 58 EN source posts corrupted), recovered in two attempts, the second of which triggered the still-standing architecture decision that blog content edits happen in a local Excel workbook first and Supabase is only ever updated via one deliberate bulk import — never via direct parallel agent writes. That decision governs every `blog_map.xlsx` recovery entry elsewhere in this changelog but was never written down. Preserved verbatim at [docs/blog-content-pipeline-history-2026-03.md](docs/blog-content-pipeline-history-2026-03.md) and the architecture decision backfilled as [ADR-0083](docs/adr/0083-excel-as-source-of-truth-for-blog-content-pipeline.md).

**Process takeaway:** documents written under `temp-files/` during a working session need an explicit "promote to `docs/` or vault before the session ends" step — `.gitignore` silently strips `temp-files/**/*.md`, so anything meant to outlive the session has to leave that directory.

- **Bug caught and fixed during that verification:** `evidence_cards` is a jsonb array holding one markdown string, not a jsonb-wrapped string like `relationships`/`host_guide` — the first pass silently skipped it in both the transform and the verify scan, so a removed character's name survived untouched while the function still reported `verified`. Fixed for all jsonb fields, not just this one.

Deleted both immediately; confirmed zero rows remain. Both client files were temporarily hand-edited to complete the walkthrough, then reverted (confirmed via `git diff`, zero changes remain in either). ### Update: guest-dropout adaptation — real Sonnet 5 prose-smoothing pass, pick-then-pay confirmed, Extras tab + lightbox (ADR-0082, staging only)
Owner review of the first pass above led to three more changes, same day:

### Fix: Kommetjie Coconut Club Mystery stuck in `needs_review` — role-only defect, misdiagnosed as missing content first (ADR-0079)
Customer `alib.botha@gmail.com` purchased "The Kommetjie Coconut Club Mystery" (8 players) at 07:43:51 UTC; generation landed `needs_review` 13 minutes later. All 8 characters had `character_role` coerced to the ADR-0052 sentinel `'invalid_role'`.
- **Misdiagnosis, corrected mid-investigation**: initially read as missing round content because `round2_script`/`round3_script`/`round4_script`/`final_statement` (the *unified* format) were empty — but this mystery is a random-slip, no-accomplice, no-fixed-murderer character-style game, which uses the *branching* format (`round2_innocent`/`round2_guilty`, etc.) instead. Those columns were already fully populated and correct, matching a same-shape reference package almost exactly. **`character_role` was the only actual defect.**
- **Two webhook re-fires turned out to be unnecessary** (~$2.40 combined, approved in advance): fired before the format mixup was caught, both regenerated already-correct content a second/third time without touching the role field.
- **The actual fix**: `UPDATE mystery_characters SET character_role = 'suspect' WHERE ... character_role = 'invalid_role'` (matching the reference package's convention), then `package_completion_blocking_defects()` confirmed clean and `promote_complete_packages()` flipped the package to `completed` immediately. Package is now live for the customer.
- **Real, separate bug found and fixed along the way**: `notify-generation-issue`'s own inline quick-recovery loop filters on `!c.description || !c.character_role` — `'invalid_role'` is a non-empty string, so the filter treated all 8 characters as "already fine" and never attempted a re-fire, silently. Patched to `!c.description || !c.character_role || c.character_role === "invalid_role"`. Deployed `notify-generation-issue` v14 → v15 (`verify_jwt: true` preserved).
- Full record, including the misdiagnosis cost, in [ADR-0079](docs/adr/0079-invalid-role-sentinel-invisible-to-auto-recovery-filter.md).

### Feature: hard quality guarantee — never show a customer defective content during the self-heal window (ADR-0077)
Pure frontend change. Previously `MysteryView.tsx` revealed a package's content as soon as it had all four content fields present, treating `completed` and `needs_review` identically — the ~10-minute silent window only suppressed the amber warning banner, not the content itself. That meant a customer opening their mystery in the first few minutes after an ADR-0053 completion-gate hold could see the exact defect the gate flagged (contaminated identity, a slipped culprit reveal, a raw template artifact) before ADR-0061's self-heal worker (5-minute worst-case repair) ever got a chance to run.
- **New `needsReviewWithinWindow`** (`MysteryView.tsx`, computed once via `useMemo`): `needs_review` **and** `needs_review_at` non-null **and** age under the existing `NEEDS_REVIEW_SILENT_WINDOW_MS` (10 min, unchanged). While true, `MysteryPackageTabView` does not render — the building screen shows instead, regardless of whether the underlying fields already look complete. `completed` is unaffected — revealed immediately, still fully trusted. `needs_review` past the window still reveals with the existing warning banner, unchanged.
- **New 5th "Final quality checks" phase in `GenerationProgress.tsx`**, gated on a new `finalizing` prop (fed `needsReviewWithinWindow`). Active only once phases 1–4 are done and `finalizing` is true; displayed progress holds in a 95→98 band, never claiming 100 until actually `completed`. Auto-bypasses to `done`/100 in the same render for any package that never passes through `needs_review` (the ordinary happy path) — no artificial delay added to the clean completion path.
- **Edge case, decided explicitly**: `needs_review` with `needs_review_at == null` (shouldn't happen post-ADR-0058, but not assumed to hold forever) evaluates `needsReviewWithinWindow = false` — reveals immediately with the existing warning rather than trapping the customer forever. Missing-images-only holds are `needs_review` too and legitimately gate for up to 10 minutes under this decision — accepted, see ADR.
- i18n: `generationProgress.phases.finalChecks.label`/`.description` added to all 13 locale files.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean (incl. sitemap/blog prerender steps).
- Full record in [ADR-0077](docs/adr/0077-frontend-hard-quality-guarantee-needs-review-gate.md).

### Fix: health-check retries transient Supabase API errors instead of alerting on them
Before deciding whether to build ADR-0075's autonomous detector-fix loop, backtested the full 56-comment history of GitHub issue #3. Found the largest single source of noise wasn't a detector bug at all: 29 of 56 comments were "Could not query ... Supabase API error" — the workflow's `api()` helper (`.github/workflows/health-check.yml`) does a bare `curl -sf` with zero retry, so any transient Supabase API blip surfaced as a false alarm.
- **Fix:** added `--retry 3 --retry-delay 5` to the curl call. Only retries curl's built-in transient set (connection errors, 408/429/500/502/503/504) — a genuine 401/403/404 still fails immediately, unchanged from before.
- **Decision on ADR-0075:** held for now. The backtest validated the core mechanical-vs-judgment classification idea (it would have correctly kept content-quality alerts like identity contamination, structural defects, and self-directed-questions escalate-only) but also surfaced that the drafted rule's "never touch package-adjacent tables" exclusion would incorrectly block automating evidence-image retries, which the codebase already trusts an existing worker (ADR-0051/0066) to do autonomously. This fix — near-zero risk, no new tables, no classifier — resolves the majority of historical noise on its own; the full loop is deferred pending evidence it's still needed after this and the acknowledgment-table fix above.

### Improvement: blanket Claude Sonnet 5 upgrade across the generation pipeline (ADR-0074)
Following the Haiku confession-leak finding (ADR-0067 follow-up), asked whether a blanket Sonnet upgrade — every Anthropic call, not just Child Calls 4/5 — would be worth it and not cost much more. Pulled a real cost estimate from actual blueprint prompt sizes plus real production content lengths and volume in Supabase before deciding, rather than guessing: current narrow-Sonnet setup ~$0.69/generation, blanket Sonnet ~$1.23-1.84/generation depending on pricing window, ~+$10-21/month at real volume (26 completed generations/month). Immaterial at current sales volume, so proceeded with the full blanket upgrade.
- **`Parent51`** (from `Parent50`): all 28 Anthropic calls (7 call-types × 4 mystery-type/style routes) `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` → `claude-sonnet-5`.
- **`Child (Unified)22`** (from `Child (Unified)21`): remaining 6 Haiku calls (Calls 1-3, both routes) → `claude-sonnet-5`. Calls 4/5 were already on Sonnet 5 from ADR-0067.
- **`Child (Detective-Style)3`** (from `Child (Detective-Style)2`): its one call, upgraded from a deprecated `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` snapshot → `claude-sonnet-5`.
- **Bug caught and fixed along the way:** while inspecting every call's full parameter set, found `temperature: 0.7` set on Child v21's Calls 4/5 (already on Sonnet 5, not yet imported to Make.com) — Sonnet 5 rejects any non-default sampling parameter with a 400, so those two calls would have broken outright on import. Stripped `temperature` from all 8 Child calls and the Detective-Style call as part of the same edit.
- Verified every file with a full recursive, type-aware structural diff against its source — each diff showed only the intended `model`/`temperature`/`name` changes.
- **Not yet imported into Make.com.** Production is still running `Parent49`/`Child19` — pre-dates even the ADR-0067 confession-split work. Import and end-to-end re-test still pending.
- **Correction (same day):** Jonathan clarified he only runs Parent + Child (Unified) live. Confirmed against `Parent50`'s JSON — all 4 routes (detective and char-based alike) send their per-character webhook call to the exact same URL, which is Child (Unified)'s trigger; no other webhook URL exists in the file. `Child (Detective-Style)` is a pre-unification leftover (see "Child Scenario Unification & Parent Fix", Apr 2026), not invoked by anything live. **`Child (Detective-Style)3` should not be imported** — live scope for this upgrade is `Parent51` + `Child (Unified)22` only, which already cover both mystery styles.
- **Correction 2 (same day): first end-to-end Sonnet 5 test failed, root cause was Make.com's `textResponse` field, not the prompts.** Real test run (Parent51 + Child22, 5-character test conversation): Parent completed cleanly on Sonnet 5, but Child characters landed with wildly inconsistent partial/empty content. Root-caused via `parse-claude-json` edge function logs: ~90% of calls returned `422 "Empty input"`. A side-by-side comparison confirmed the Anthropic call itself succeeded with a complete, valid response every time — but Make's `{{callId.textResponse}}` convenience field (feeding the Parse step's body) evaluated to empty regardless, a Make.com "Anthropic Claude" connector bug specific to `claude-sonnet-5` responses. **Fix:** all 8 Parse Claude JSON modules' body changed from `{{callId.textResponse}}` to `{{callId.content[].text}}` (raw content-array access, confirmed reliable) → shipped as `Child (Unified)23`.
- **Correction 3 (same day): residual Call 3/4 failures were a real `parse-claude-json` bug, not another Make quirk.** Re-test of v23 still failed 50-75% of Call 3 (Innocent Scripts) and Call 4 (Guilty Scripts) specifically. A pre-Parse-delay theory (`Child (Unified)24`, 2s Sleep before each Parse step, in case of a Make bundle-materialization race) didn't help — the next run was worse, and the failure pattern by call position ruled out a simple timing race. Pulled the actual failing bundle: `stop_reason: "end_turn"` (ruled out `max_tokens` truncation), but the response had one raw, unescaped newline byte inside a JSON string value (Sonnet 5 occasionally emits a literal line break instead of the `\n` escape sequence) — `parse-claude-json`'s sanitizer had no stage for this. **Fix:** added a string-aware `escapeControlCharsInStrings()` stage to `supabase/functions/parse-claude-json/index.ts` (tracks JSON string-open/close state, only touches control bytes inside strings — a first naive global-replace attempt broke on the response's own pretty-printed structural newlines, caught in a local test harness before deploying). Verified against 4 cases including the real failing input, then deployed (v6→v7) and re-confirmed live via direct curl against the exact real payload — `200`, all fields recovered, zero Anthropic spend for verification. `Child (Unified)24`'s delay is superseded; no blueprint change needed since the fix lives entirely in the Supabase function. One more small test still needed to confirm the overall rate.
- Full record in [ADR-0074](docs/adr/0074-blanket-sonnet-5-upgrade-across-generation-pipeline.md).

### Correction (ADR-0070): the actual live detective-style prompt is inside Child (Unified), not the standalone Detective-Style blueprint — root-cause fix rebuilt in the right place
ADR-0070's staged fix (`Child (Detective-Style)2/3`) targeted the wrong scenario. Confirmed independently of the correction already logged above (same root fact, different investigation thread): `Child (Detective-Style)` is a pre-unification leftover, not invoked by anything live — Parent calls one webhook for all 4 routes, and that webhook is `Child (Unified)`. Unified has its own internal detective-style prompt track (modules 401/405/409, "Call 1-3"), completely independent text from the standalone file, never kept in sync with it.
- **Real root cause, found in module 409 ("Call 3: Round Scripts"), the only call that outputs `finalStatement`:** two separate defects, both more precise than the "recency bias" theory ADR-0070 originally proposed against the wrong file. (1) `content_coherence_rules`' ACCOMPLICE COHERENCE rule reads "NEVER script the accomplice to accuse, incriminate, or turn on the murderer in any round" — no exception for `finalStatement`, so the model has a standing instruction against the accomplice ever admitting anything. (2) The `finalStatement` schema field's bracketed guidance only distinguishes murderer vs. "innocents" — it never mentions accomplice behavior at all, so accomplice output falls through to defect (1) with nothing to override it. Together these fully explain the "murderer confesses and names the accomplice, accomplice denies it anyway" pattern found in ADR-0070's sample.
- **Fix shipped as `Child (Unified)25-DetectiveFinalStatementFix`** (built on today's `24-PreParseDelay`, verified via structural diff to touch only module 409): the ACCOMPLICE COHERENCE rule now explicitly scopes the "never turn on the murderer" instruction to Rounds 2-4 and states the reverse for `finalStatement`; the `finalStatement` schema field now gives murderer/accomplice/suspect each their own explicit instruction (previously accomplice had none); added a post-schema self-check telling the model to re-read its own `finalStatement` for denial language before finishing, same technique as ADR-0067's fix. Not yet imported into Make.com.
- **Not superseded:** the detector (`list_packages_with_unconfessed_culprit`) and the 14 hand-patched paid packages from ADR-0070 are unaffected by this correction — those were direct DB content fixes, independent of which blueprint generates future content.
- Full record in [ADR-0070](docs/adr/0070-detective-style-culprit-final-statement-unreliable-confession.md) (updated with this correction).

### Fix + verified live: detective-style final-statement fix tested end-to-end, one regression caught and fixed (ADR-0070 follow-up)
Live-tested `Child (Unified)25` by calling the child webhook directly (bypassing Parent) against a disposable test package (`is_test=true`, `f0f0fa7a-...`, never a real customer) — a 3-character detective mystery built specifically to exercise the murderer/accomplice final-statement path.
- **First test run failed differently than expected:** both characters' Call 3 hit `parse-claude-json` 422s ("Unterminated string in JSON"). Diagnosed via raw Make execution log: both Anthropic responses were missing their closing `"}`, cut off right after a complete, well-formed final sentence, with `stop_reason: "end_turn"` — not a token-limit truncation. Root cause: a self-check instruction added in the same edit ("before finalizing, re-read finalStatement... rewrite it if needed") gave the model an extra review step positioned exactly where it needed to close out the JSON instead — plausibly causing it to treat the self-check as the last task and never emit the closing syntax. 2-for-2 failure, not random flakiness.
- **Fix:** `Child (Unified)26-DropSelfCheckTruncationFix` (built on 25, structural diff confirms only this one instruction changed) — replaced the self-check with a plain "close the string and object immediately, no review step" instruction.
- **Re-tested against the same two characters — clean pass.** Both landed fully in the DB (round2-4 scripts + final_statement all populated), and the content is exactly right: Vivian (murderer) gives a full confession naming Tom's specific help; Tom (accomplice) gives a full admission naming Vivian as the killer — no denial, no deflection.
- **`Child (Unified)26` is the version to import/keep live, not 25.** The underlying content fixes (accomplice-coherence carve-out, finalStatement role guidance) are unchanged and now confirmed working by a real end-to-end test, not just a diff review.
- Test package left in place (`is_test=true`, excluded from all detectors/customer views per ADR-0072) rather than deleted, for reference.
- Full record in [ADR-0070](docs/adr/0070-detective-style-culprit-final-statement-unreliable-confession.md).

### Fix: bracket-wrapped reserve/placeholder roster lines counted as real characters
Follow-up alert after the two false alarms above: "Death At The Birthday Bash: A Speakeasy Soirée Turned Deadly" flagged approved=22, actual=17. Investigation found this one is genuinely mixed — part detector noise, part real gap. The approved concept message itself is truncated mid-generation (cuts off "If Jessica cannot attend, her" with no closing sentence, no Murder Method section). Its last two numbered lines are leftover placeholder text the model invented while trying to fill "two more maybe characters" slots the customer only answered one of: `21. **[RESERVE CHARACTER - Brian's Alternate]** – If Brian cannot attend, his character's secrets and motives will be redistributed among the other suspects.` These match `characterLineRegex`/`boldCharRegex` structurally (bold name + separator + description) but aren't real characters, inflating the "approved" count from 20 real named people to 22.
- **Fix:** added `isPlaceholderCharacterName()` (name starts with `[`) and applied it at all 4 character-capture sites in `extractRosterFromMessage`/`extractCharactersFromMessages` — same "match structure, not literal wording" principle as ADR-0063/ADR-0068. Regression test added to `scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs`. Verified against the real message content: the extractor now returns 20, not 22.
- **The real gap underneath, left open:** even at the true count of 20, only 17 characters were actually delivered (`mystery_packages.extracted_characters` already only had 17 clean names at generation time, weeks ago). Missing: Mikey "Annie" Sinchai and Dr. Addison "Add" Sinchai (both explicitly requested "leaves early" guests, not optional) and Jessica Thorne (tagged "MAYBE ATTENDING" but never withdrawn by the customer). Likely cause: the approved message's truncation forced the Claude-fallback extraction path, whose `relevantContent.substring(0, 8000)` truncation (flagged as an unfixed risk in ADR-0069, candidate fix #3) plausibly cut off before reaching these characters' details in the chat history.
- **Investigated for customer impact, inconclusive from data alone:** no support contact, no guest_feedback/mystery_feedback rows, no character_assignments made through the app for this package (`733b02dd-...`, paid, generated 2026-07-20 — a real 46th-birthday party, presumably already held). This package already had one prior unrelated hand-fix (missing evidence image, 2026-08-02).
- **Resolved (2026-08-11): no further action.** Jonathan already emailed the customer on 2026-08-08 asking clarifying questions about the package — no reply as of today, 3 days later. Decision: leave as-is for now rather than proactively hand-write the 3 missing characters or re-send outreach; revisit only if the customer responds or a new signal (review, support ticket) surfaces.

### Fix: two health-check false alarms — ADR-0063/ADR-0068 fix never pushed, confession-leak detector had no negation guard
Morning health-check run flagged two problems on issue #3: a roster-count mismatch on "The Host Herself" (approved=11, actual=12) and a confession leak in the Final Statements round on "The Host Herself" (Cameron/Camille Voss) and "Murder At Camp Pine Shadow" (Pixie Lens). Both turned out to be false alarms, for two unrelated reasons.

**Roster mismatch — the ADR-0063/ADR-0068 fixes were documented as shipped in this file but never actually committed.** `CHANGELOG.md` already carried write-ups for both (2026-08-05, 2026-08-07) and both linked to ADR files, but `git status` showed `supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts`, `scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs`, and the ADR-0063/ADR-0068 markdown files themselves sitting uncommitted in the working tree the whole time. The health-check workflow re-parses each approved snapshot with the *committed* `main` source (`scripts/detect-roster-mismatches.mjs`), so it kept running the old pre-fix regex against Heather's already-correctly-hand-patched 12-character package and finding a phantom 11-vs-12 mismatch. Verified against the real DB message content that the working-tree extractor already returns 12 (matching actual); pushed the fix (commit `29e744b`) so `main` — and CI — now match what the changelog already claimed.
- **Not a new customer issue.** All 12 characters, including Blaire/Blair Ashford, are correctly in `mystery_characters` for conversation `ac2c3610-...` — this was purely a "the fix exists but was never pushed" gap.

**Confession-leak false positive — `list_packages_with_final_statement_confession_leak` had no negation guard.** The detector's regex (`\mI (did it|killed|poisoned|...)\M`) matched the confession phrase embedded inside a denial: Cameron/Camille Voss's final statement says "...None of that means **I did it**," and Pixie Lens's says "...doesn't mean **I poisoned** anyone." Both `final_guilty` fields are correct, in-character denials per ADR-0067's design; the real confessions are properly isolated in `reveal_confession_guilty`. Same failure class already documented for the sibling detective-style detector in ADR-0070.
- **Fix:** added an `AND NOT` negation guard (matches this migration file's existing `murderer_flags`/`accomplice_flags` pattern) — excludes a confession-verb match if a negation word (doesn't/didn't/isn't/wasn't/won't/wouldn't/none/nothing) appears within 5 words before it. See [migration](supabase/migrations/20260811_fix_confession_leak_negation_false_positive.sql).
- **Applied directly to production** (`mhfikaomkmqcndqfohbp`) and verified: `list_packages_with_final_statement_confession_leak()` now returns zero rows. Checked the guard doesn't blanket-suppress true positives — at time of fix these were the only two rows the detector had ever matched, so there was no existing true positive to regress.

### Fix: purchase-preview character parser was English-only, blocking non-English checkout (ADR-0073)
Customer (pt) reported "Não conseguimos detectar sua lista de personagens" while trying to finish checkout, with the checkout button itself replaced by a "back to design" prompt. Her approved concept was well-formed (`## Lista de Personagens (6 jogadores)` followed by 6 clean numbered characters) — the bug was that `parseCharacters()` in [MysteryPurchase.tsx](src/pages/MysteryPurchase.tsx) only recognized English section headers ("CHARACTER LIST", "Characters", "SUSPECTS"), so a Portuguese (or any non-English) header never matched and the parser returned zero characters, which both showed the warning and hid the checkout button ([MysteryPurchase.tsx:667](src/pages/MysteryPurchase.tsx#L667)). The actual generation backend (`mystery-webhook-trigger`) already handled this correctly via a 13-locale header list plus a header-agnostic fallback (ADR-0057) — this was the same "paired-predicate drift" pattern as before, just in a client-side parser that never got the same fix.
- `parseCharacters()` now falls back to a header-agnostic scan (4+ consecutive numbered/bold `**Name** – description` lines) when no English header section matches, instead of returning an empty array. Mirrors the edge function's existing batch-path approach rather than duplicating its 26-entry locale header list (avoids reintroducing the same drift risk).
- Verified against the customer's actual message content: correctly extracts all 6 characters and does not pick up the single isolated "Vítima" bold line as a false character.
- No backfill needed — this blocks checkout pre-payment, so no customer has a corrupted package from it.
- Full record in [ADR-0073](docs/adr/0073-purchase-preview-parser-english-only-header-blocked-non-english-checkout.md).

New nullable `conversations.purchaser_first_name` column, not yet populated (stripe-webhook capture is a deferred follow-up, see below).

Until the webhook change ships, the popup shows real recent purchases with "A customer just purchased" (no name).

## 2026-08-08

### Found + fixed: detective-style Final Statements round unreliably reveals the culprit (ADR-0070)
Support check on a specific paid order ("Death At The Blackthorn Wedding", `cd4ca44d-...`, `princesslea82886@gmail.com`, $24.99, purchased 2026-08-07) first looked like a recurrence of ADR-0067, but that package is `mystery_style='detective'` — a format ADR-0067 explicitly didn't touch. Detective-style has no separate "Reveal" round; "Final Statements" *is* the reveal moment, and the murderer's `final_statement` is supposed to branch by role into a confession/admission/denial per the Make.com "MM Live - Child (Detective-Style)" blueprint. That branching turned out to be unreliable at the content level, not just cosmetic: in a meaningful share of packages the murderer's own final statement is a flat denial instead of a confession, or the murderer confesses and names an accomplice who then denies it in their own statement — same round, direct contradiction. Ran a keyword heuristic across all 60 completed detective-style packages and manually verified every hit: **15 flagged, all paid, purchases spanning 2026-04-22 through 2026-08-07** (11 murderer-denies, 4 accomplice-denies-despite-named). One confirmed false positive ("Death At The Velvet Rose") documented in the detector.
- **Detector shipped:** `list_packages_with_unconfessed_culprit()` (`supabase/migrations/20260808_detect_unconfessed_detective_culprit.sql`), same read-only/escalate-only pattern as `list_packages_with_identity_conflicts` (ADR-0041). Deployed and verified live.
- **Root-cause fix staged:** `temp-files/MM Live - Child (Detective-Style)2-ReliableCulpritConfession.blueprint.json`. Diagnosis: the model reliably determines role correctly (verified `master_context.murdererSelection.character` matches `character_name` exactly on a bad sample — this isn't a name-matching bug) but doesn't reliably carry that role through to the `finalStatement` field, most likely because everything generated just before it (Rounds 2-4) explicitly instructs the murderer/accomplice to actively lie, and nothing pushes back against that momentum at the one field where it's supposed to reverse — same failure shape ADR-0067 found in the sibling call. Fix: 5 targeted prompt edits (verified as the only diff via structural JSON compare) — explicit "STOP DECEIVING HERE" / "this is an ADMISSION, not a denial" callouts on the murderer/accomplice Final Statement instructions, an anti-default-header instruction on the `finalStatement` output template, a qualified (not blanket) "lying throughout" reminder in `<critical_reminders>`, and a self-check instruction telling the model to re-read its own output for denial language before finishing. **Not yet imported/activated in Make.com** — staged only, per this project's standing blueprint convention (duplicate-and-stage, deploy is a separate manual step).
- **14 of 15 affected paid customers hand-patched** (skipped the 1 confirmed false positive): wrote corrected `final_statement` content for each affected murderer/accomplice — full confessions or admissions, in-character, sourced from each character's own `background`/`secret`/`relationships` fields and cross-checked against their counterpart's statement for consistency (e.g. Sinclair Pemberton's admission matches the specifics Marlowe Sterling's confession already attributed to him). One case ("Morte No Topo") was a single-sentence contradiction fix, not a rewrite — the confession content was already correct, just preceded by a leftover denial line. All content hand-authored directly, no metered API calls, per standing policy. Re-ran the detector after patching: all 14 confirmed-bad packages cleared. 3 rows remain flagged (the known "Velvet Rose" false positive, plus two new false-positive surfacings on "Ghosts Of The Past" and "The Case Of The Stolen Golden Flamingo" — both because the corrected murderer confessions now explicitly name their accomplice, and the accomplice's own already-fine statement doesn't hit the detector's admission keyword list). No customer outreach performed — patched data only.
- **Not yet done:** importing/activating the staged blueprint fix in Make.com, wiring the detector into `.github/workflows/health-check.yml` (there's an in-progress, uncommitted check 12 for roster-count drift already in that file from a separate workstream — this would be check 13, added without disturbing it), and any decision on proactive customer outreach for the patched packages.
- Full record in [ADR-0070](docs/adr/0070-detective-style-culprit-final-statement-unreliable-confession.md).

### Found (not yet fixed): `approved_concept_message_id` never re-captures after a later roster revision (ADR-0069)
While sweeping paid packages for other ADR-0068 instances, found "Death At The Blackthorn Wedding" (`cd4ca44d-...`) with a 12-vs-10 roster mismatch that initially looked like a second ADR-0068 case (its roster lines use `(Female)`/`(Male)` tags between name and dash, same shape as `*(OPTIONAL PLAYER)*`) — confirmed the deployed regex does garble it and the ADR-0068 fix does correctly parse all 12. But that's not what generated the actual package: `approved_concept_message_id` points to a **2026-07-22** message; the customer explicitly revised to "ten players" on **2026-08-07**, 16 days later, in the conversation's final message — `player_count` synced to 10 correctly, but the snapshot pointer never moved. Generation ran against the stale 12-player draft; a regex-garble → Claude-fallback detour (which truncates all-drafts-concatenated content to 8000 chars, likely never reaching her actual final message) produced 10 characters that are the first 10 names of the **stale** draft, not her actual final revision.
- **Root cause:** `approved_concept_message_id` capture guard in `mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts` is `if (!conversation.approved_concept_message_id ...)` — captured once, never re-evaluated against later messages that supersede it.
- **Independent of ADR-0068:** deploying that fix alone doesn't resolve this — it would clean up the symptom (regex would parse the stale snapshot correctly) without fixing the actual bug (wrong message treated as ground truth).
- **Deferred per explicit instruction:** documented now (ADR-0069, 3 candidate fix approaches listed, not yet evaluated against each other), implementation and this customer's remediation left for separate follow-up work. No sweep run yet for other packages with the same drift pattern.
