### Fix: `characterLineRegex` dropped roster lines with an inline annotation between name and dash (ADR-0068)
Root-cause fix for the incident in the entry below. `characterLineRegex` and `boldCharRegex` in `supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts` (three call sites: the primary header-path parser, the header-agnostic batch path, and the secondary/legacy consecutive-bold-lines fallback) required the separator (`-–—:`) to follow the character name immediately after only whitespace. A line like `**Blaire/Blair Ashford** *(OPTIONAL PLAYER)* – ...` has an italic parenthetical between the name and the separator and silently failed to match, while every unannotated line on the same roster matched fine — no error, no count signal, just a short roster.
- **Fix:** added an optional `(?:\s*\*?\([^)]*\)\*?)?` group between the name capture and the separator in all three regex declarations, tolerating any short parenthetical aside (italicized or not) without needing to special-case the literal wording "OPTIONAL PLAYER" — matches structure, not text, same principle as ADR-0063's fix in this same file.
- **Verified:** live regex test against the customer's exact approved line (real en-dash separator) — now matches, captures the correct name (not the annotation), and the annotation itself is dropped from the description. Confirmed no regression against all previously-passing cases (plain dash, colon, unbolded names, non-character lines).
- **Regression test added:** `scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs` — new check using the customer's actual roster shape (11 unannotated + 1 annotated line), transpiling and running the real shipped source per this file's existing ADR-0057/ADR-0063 discipline. All 12 checks in the suite pass.
- **Not done in this pass:** a sweep for other paid packages whose approved concept snapshot has a similar bracketed/italic annotation on a numbered roster line, and wiring `conceptSnapshot.test.mjs` into CI (it's currently run manually, same as before this change).
- Full record in [ADR-0068](docs/adr/0068-roster-annotation-breaks-character-line-regex.md).

### Fix: 12th "optional player" character silently dropped from a paid package ("The Host Herself", `ac2c3610-...`)
Customer (Heather, `heather.aadb@outlook.com`) explicitly asked mid-chat for a 12th "optional player" character ("if they do not come it would not ruin the game"), the assistant proposed and built one in ("Blaire/Blair Ashford"), she approved the concept with `12. **Blaire/Blair Ashford** *(OPTIONAL PLAYER)*` in the roster, and paid 20 minutes later. `mystery_characters` only had 11 rows — Blaire never generated.
- **Root cause, confirmed by regex test:** `characterLineRegex` in `supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts` requires the bolded name to be followed immediately (after optional whitespace) by a `-–—:` separator. The italic `*(OPTIONAL PLAYER)*` annotation between Blaire's name and the dash breaks that match — item 11 matches, item 12 doesn't — so the header-path parse silently returns 11 characters instead of 12. `extracted_characters` on the package confirmed exactly 11 entries, no Blaire, matching the diagnosis. This is a sibling of ADR-0063's fix (a different literal trigger — an inline annotation, not a subheading) and was **not** caught by ADR-0064's guardrail, because that guardrail targets the model *inventing* an unrequested optional tier, not a customer explicitly requesting one that the parser then can't read. Detector functions (`list_packages_with_structural_defects` etc.) didn't flag it either — roster-count drift is checked by a separate Node script (`scripts/detect-roster-mismatches.mjs`), not the SQL detectors.
- **Also flagged by the same request:** this package was generated on the pre-ADR-0067 blueprint (v49/v18, during the revert-and-retest window), so all characters had the same "final_guilty is a full unconditional confession" bug ADR-0067 fixed.
- **Fix applied (hand-patch, not regenerate):** wrote Blaire's full character record directly — background, secret, relationships, rumors, accusations, all 4 rounds (innocent/guilty branches + questions), final statement, and the new reveal-confession split — consistent with the other 11 characters' established voice, motive, and the package's canon (murder window, evidence, spa-robe security footage). Her guilty branch resolves the "arrived at 5:15 PM" claim as a fabricated alibi (she was actually on-site since ~2 PM), consistent with two other characters' existing suspicion of her convenient timing.
- **Also applied the ADR-0067 split to all 12 characters in this package** (not just Blaire): each existing character's old `final_guilty` (a full confession, headed "Final Statement") was moved into the new `reveal_confession_guilty` field (header changed to "The Reveal — Your Confession"; body content already satisfied the confession spec verbatim, per ADR-0067's own note that "it just never had real content to point at before"), and a new proper denial was written into `final_guilty` for each character, matching their established voice and the same admit-motive/deny-the-act structure already used in rounds 2-4.
- **Package-level consistency fixes:** `detective_script`'s suspect count ("eleven suspects" → "twelve suspects") and its Final Statements narration (removed "or, if you are the person I believe you are, you can begin to crack" — contradicted the now-denial-only Final Statements round). `extracted_characters` and `conversations.player_count` (11 → 12) updated to match.
- **All content hand-authored directly (not via a metered API call)** — no Anthropic/OpenAI keys used, per standing policy.
- **Verified clean:** all 9 SQL content-quality/structural detectors (`list_packages_with_structural_defects`, `list_completed_but_empty_packages`, `list_packages_missing_evidence_images`, `list_packages_with_evidence_culprit_spoiler`, `list_packages_with_identity_conflicts`, `list_packages_with_meta_text_leak`, `list_packages_with_self_directed_questions`, `list_packages_with_slip_culprit_leak`, `list_packages_with_victim_mismatch`, `list_packages_with_victim_as_character`) re-run after the edits, all empty.
- **Not yet done:** the underlying regex bug in `characterLineRegex` (tracked separately — see next entry) and a sweep for other paid packages hit by the same "annotation between name and dash" pattern.

### Fix: split character-style "Final Statement" into a Final-Statements denial and a separate Reveal confession (ADR-0067)
Raleigh (same customer as ADR-0063/0064) followed up: *"the character scripts have the final statement of the murderer as a confession so that would indicate no reveal... Am I reading it wrong?"* She wasn't. Checked her package plus 3 other paid character-style packages — systemic, not a one-off: every `final_guilty`/`final_accomplice` field is headed `## FINAL STATEMENT` (matching the Final Statements round) and is a full unconditional confession, with no staging cue about timing — but the AI-generated `detective_script`'s "THE REVEAL" section (the *next* round) is written assuming the confession hasn't happened yet (`[The murderer reads their confession aloud]`). Two independently-generated pieces of content disagreed about when the confession happens.
- **Explicit bar for the fix:** no improvisation, ever, at any `script_type` — a "hold this back when you get there" instruction was rejected; the fix had to be structural.

New `reveal_confession_guilty`/`reveal_confession_accomplice` columns carry the actual confession, used only when the Detective calls on that player during The Reveal — exactly the moment the detective script's cue already expected.
- **Root cause traced to a self-contradiction within one Make.com prompt:** "Call 4: Guilty Scripts" instructs rounds 2-4 to deny, but `finalGuilty`'s own schema line broke that pattern ("the dramatic reveal moment"). Fixed in duplicated blueprints (`temp-files/`, per convention — never edit the current version in place): `Child (Unified)19` → `Child (Unified)20-RevealConfessionSplit`, `Parent49` → `Parent50 (Reveal-Confession Split)`. Verified via full structural diff that only the intended strings changed (a 4.5MB→2.8MB size drop on the Parent file was confirmed to be a pure UTF-8/whitespace re-serialization artifact, not data loss).
- **Also updated:** `generate-pointform-summaries` (new fields added to its dynamic field list — no other change needed), `MysteryPackageTabView.tsx` (new fields rendered, `ROUND_INTENT` hints corrected so the Final Statements hint no longer says "or, if you're guilty, make your confession"), `HostGuideTemplate.tsx` (Final Statements description and the "don't confess too early" tip now spell out the two-stage structure for character-based mysteries), `mysteryPackageService.ts` and `src/interfaces/mystery.ts` (new fields wired through).

- **Not yet live:** the two edited blueprints are staged in `temp-files/` only — deploying/activating them in Make.com is a separate step. **Not in scope generally:** backfilling other already-completed packages; detective-style (predetermined-culprit) mysteries, which weren't affected.
- Migration: `supabase/migrations/20260806_add_reveal_confession_fields.sql`.

## 2026-08-05

### Fix: optional characters silently dropped from generated package (ADR-0063)
Customer (Raleigh, "Murder At Camp Pine Shadow"/"Camp Purgatory Pines", `fa8ba43a-...`) reported the AI promised optional bonus characters would be included, then they weren't. Confirmed: her approved concept snapshot listed 15 core characters under `## Character List (15 players)` plus 3 more under `### Optional Characters (for 16-18 players)`; only the 15 core characters made it into `mystery_characters`, and `player_count` silently synced down to 15 with no signal to her that anything was dropped.
- **Root cause:** `extractRosterFromMessage` in `supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts` stopped parsing at the first `##`/`###` heading that wasn't on its `CHARACTER_LIST_HEADERS` allow-list. `### Optional Characters (for 16-18 players)` isn't on that list, so parsing broke there even though more valid numbered character entries followed.
- **Fix:** the stop condition is now structural instead of text-based — on hitting an unrecognized subheading, it peeks at the next non-blank line and only stops if that line does *not* look like a character entry. A message-worded subheading like "Optional Characters" (or any future wording/locale) no longer needs to be enumerated by hand; the parser follows the roster's shape, not the model's wording for it. Verified against Raleigh's real message: now extracts all 18 characters (was 15), and still correctly stops at `## Murder Method` afterward.
- **Scope check:** queried all paid conversations whose approved concept snapshot mentions "Optional Characters" — only Raleigh's was affected; the one other match (`f106ef2c-...`, 20 players) had a matching character count, unaffected.
- **Not fixed in this pass:** in-app character rename doesn't propagate the new name across round scripts/clues/host guide text (only updates `mystery_characters.character_name`). Also reported by the same customer; tracked separately, see vault note.
- Full record in [ADR-0063](docs/adr/0063-structural-roster-continuation-parsing.md).

### Feature: prevent and detect roster-count drift (ADR-0064)
Follow-up to the fix above. Investigating *why* Raleigh's concept snapshot had an "optional characters" section found that it isn't a real feature — checked every chat prompt branch and there's no instruction, schema column, or UI backing a core/optional character split. The model invented it and promised something the product has no mechanism to deliver. Two controls added:
- **Prevention:** a guardrail directive is now appended unconditionally to `systemPrompt` in `supabase/functions/mystery-ai/index.ts`, after all branch logic runs — covering the `MYSTERY_FREE_PROMPT` external secret path too (confirmed via `supabase secrets list` that standard murder mysteries, including Raleigh's, use this external prompt in production, not the inline templates alone — editing only the inline templates would have missed the dominant case).
- **Detection:** new `scripts/detect-roster-mismatches.mjs`, wired into `health-check.yml` as check 12. Re-parses each paid completed package's approved concept snapshot with the shipped `extractRosterFromMessage` (same transpile-and-run technique as `scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs` — no second parser) and flags any mismatch against the actual `mystery_characters` count. Escalate-only, 30-day rolling window, same pattern as the existing content-quality/structural detectors.
- **Found running it against real data:** Raleigh's package still mismatches (expected, pending her regenerate). A genuinely new, unrelated bug surfaced too — "Whispers From The Void" (`ffea7320-...`) has 9 characters delivered vs. 10 approved. Not investigated in this pass; flagged for follow-up. A third case ("Death At The Velvet Viper") was a false positive from a known stale-draft incident (ADR-0048) exceeding the pipeline's 35-character cap — fixed by mirroring that same bound in the detector.
- Full record in [ADR-0064](docs/adr/0064-prevent-and-detect-roster-count-drift.md).

### Improvement: gate the generation-issue alert on the self-heal loop's outcome (ADR-0065)
The alert above fired one second after `needs_review` was set — before the self-heal loop even got a chance. Investigated `notify-generation-issue`: it's called synchronously from the completion trigger with no age gate, only a 6h anti-repeat cooldown. Recommended a hybrid gate (worker-awareness first, timer as fallback) over a pure timer or wiring the alert into the remediation worker itself; built it once the owner confirmed.
- **Gate logic** (`notify-generation-issue/index.ts`): alert immediately if the current defect(s) include any class the worker has no handler for at all (`error_body_in_package`, `error_body_in_character`, `invalid_role`, `victim_is_playable_character`); otherwise wait for either an `escalated`/`failed` row in `auto_remediation_log` since `needs_review_at` (worker gave up — alert now) or 35 minutes elapsed (one 30-min sweep + buffer), whichever comes first.
- **Deliberately coarse escalation check:** matches on *any* escalated/failed row for the package, not a specific defect class — this codebase's `structuralDefects` prefixes and the worker's `auto_remediation_log.defect_class` strings don't match 1:1 (`self_directed_question` vs `self_directed_questions`, `identity_conflict` vs `identity_contamination` — same naming-drift pattern as ADR-0056). A precise per-class mapping was fully enumerated and then rejected as a fourth instance of a bug this codebase keeps re-encountering.
- **New 10-min sweep** (`sweep_stuck_needs_review_packages()`, mirroring `sweep_incomplete_packages()`'s existing shape): re-invokes `notify-generation-issue` for every still-`needs_review` package, since the only other caller fires once, synchronously, at age-zero — without a re-check the grace-period gate could never actually pass.
- **Caught during verification, before shipping:** the sweep's first draft filtered on `is_paid = true` (matching a different function's convention) — dropped after confirming the actual completion trigger has no such filter, which would have permanently stranded unpaid packages. Also found and deleted a leftover disposable test row (`362d2b74-...`, from the 2026-08-02 ADR-0061 verification session, no matching `conversations` row) that the new sweep would have fired a spurious "Unknown"-customer email on within its first 10-minute tick.
- Full record in [ADR-0065](docs/adr/0065-gate-generation-issue-alert-on-self-heal-outcome.md).

Confirmed false-positive from an overly strict default filter, not unsafe content.
- **Customer fixed immediately:** manually regenerated Round 3 at the higher tolerance; all three evidence images now present. Logged to `auto_remediation_log` as a manual entry, same audit pattern as the 2026-08-02 precedent.
- **Autonomous fix, so this doesn't need a human next time:** `generate-evidence-images` now accepts an optional `safety_tolerance` override (defaults to 2, unchanged for existing callers). `handleMissingImages` in the worker now detects the specific `NSFW content detected` reason and retries *only* those rounds at `safety_tolerance: 5`, inside the same attempt (not a second scheduled sweep) — other failure types (network, rate-limit) are untouched, and genuinely graphic content still escalates to a human if the retry also fails.
- **No new paid-API dependency:** the fix is one extra bounded Replicate call ($0.04) on an already-approved, already-autonomous spend path — not a new capability. An LLM-based prompt-rewrite fallback (for a case that fails even at the higher tolerance) was considered and deliberately not built without asking first, since that would be a new Anthropic/Claude spend surface.
- Full record in [ADR-0066](docs/adr/0066-retry-nsfw-rejected-evidence-images-at-higher-tolerance.md).

## 2026-08-04

### Fix: Pages build failing with Postgres statement timeout during blog prerender
The GitHub Pages deploy build (`deploy.yml`) failed at `node scripts/prerender-blog.mjs` with `57014: canceling statement due to statement timeout` right after "Fetching published blog posts...".
- **Root cause 1 (the actual bug):** `deploy.yml`'s "Build project" step never set `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`, unlike every other Supabase-touching workflow in this repo. `prerender-blog.mjs`'s env-var fallback silently dropped to its hardcoded **anon** key, which carries a **3-second** `statement_timeout` — not the 8s the script's own comment assumed (8s is the `authenticated` role's limit; this script never uses that role). It's been running on the 3s cap this whole time.
- **Root cause 2 (why it was on the edge):** `fetchAllPosts()` paginates via `.eq('status','published').order('id').range(...)` against only a single-column `status` index. Confirmed via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`: with no composite index, every page forces a full fetch + sort of all 2652 published rows just to slice out 100 (~350ms/page even warm-cached) — the exact same problem that already forced a page-size cut from 500→100 once before, when the table was "1.4k+ rows." It's since nearly doubled.
- **Fixes:** (1) wired `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` into `deploy.yml`'s build step (service_role has no `statement_timeout` override) — confirmed both secrets already exist in the repo via `gh secret list`. (2) Added a composite `idx_blog_posts_status_id` index; confirmed via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` this eliminates the full-table sort entirely (349ms → 27.7ms for the same page, 12.6x). (3) Corrected the stale "8s" comment in `prerender-blog.mjs` to describe the real constraint.
- No ADR — this is a bug fix (missing CI credentials + missing index), not an architectural decision.

### Improvement: tighten the full remediation sweep from 4 hours to 30 minutes (ADR-0062)
Investigating a customer's `needs_review` package (angela.bone@unt.edu, "Birthday Betrayal In Hot Springs", `9464a4c7-...`) found a routine `self_directed_question` defect (Zach's Round 3 questions asked himself instead of another suspect) that the worker already knows how to fix for free — it just hadn't had its turn, since that class is only swept by the 4-hour full-window job, not the 5-minute held-only job ADR-0061 added. Manually invoked `auto-remediate-packages` (scoped to `classes: ["self_directed_questions"]`, dry-run first) to fix it immediately; confirmed clean via `list_packages_with_self_directed_questions()`.
- **Root cause of the wait, not just this one case:** ADR-0061 explicitly rejected tightening the full 4-hour job, reasoning it would 48x the paid classes' frequency for no benefit — spend-cap pressure. That reasoning assumed enough purchase volume for the $5/day cap to matter. Confirmed actual volume is 1-3 purchases/day, well short of that.
- **Change:** `auto-remediate-packages` cron schedule changed from `43 */4 * * *` to `13,43 * * * *` (every 30 minutes) — same job (updated in place via `cron.schedule`, confirmed same `jobid`), same scope (all six classes, all statuses), no code change. Offset keeps the original `:43` (26 min clear of the 6-hourly health check's `:17` slot) and adds `:13` (4 min before), both far outside the worker's observed ~1-11s execution time.
- Makes a narrower fix considered earlier in this investigation (adding `self_directed_questions` to the 5-minute held-only job) unnecessary — every class now gets picked up within 30 minutes regardless.
- Full record in [ADR-0062](docs/adr/0062-tighten-full-remediation-sweep-to-30-minutes.md).

## 2026-08-02

### Fix: manually recovered a round4 evidence image stuck on a Replicate NSFW rejection
"Death At The Birthday Bash: A Speakeasy Soirée Turned Deadly" (paid, `733b02dd-...`) was missing its round4 evidence-card image; the auto-remediation worker had tried twice (2026-08-01, $0.12 spent) and escalated after hitting its attempt cap. Manually re-ran `generate-evidence-images` to find the actual cause.
- **Root cause: not transient.** The round4 evidence card's `#### DESCRIPTION` — ricin extraction methodology, lethal dosage calculations, an "underground supplier" paid in Bitcoin — builds a Replicate Flux 1.1 Pro prompt that deterministically fails: `"Error generating image: NSFW content detected."` Every retry with the same prompt was always going to fail the same way; the worker's 2-attempt cap just spent $0.08 confirming that before correctly escalating.
- **Fix applied:** re-ran the same edge function by hand with a sanitized prompt — same visual concept (locked laptop folder, scattered research pages, forensic lighting) with the explicit toxin-synthesis/procurement language removed. Succeeded on the first try. The evidence card text players actually read is unchanged; only the image-generation prompt was rewritten. Logged to `auto_remediation_log` as a manual entry so the audit trail matches what the automated worker would have recorded.
- **Not fixed — a real gap, left open:** `handleMissingImages` in `auto-remediate-packages/index.ts` has no handling for a deterministic content-policy rejection; it will keep spending its attempt budget retrying an identical doomed prompt on any other package whose evidence description reads as too graphic (poison synthesis, weapon crafting, etc.) rather than recognizing the failure as non-retryable and escalating immediately with the NSFW reason surfaced. Worth a follow-up: detect the `NSFW content detected` error specifically and either skip straight to escalation (saving the wasted retry) or attempt one sanitized-prompt fallback before escalating.

### Fix: health-check needs_review alert had no grace period, false-alarmed on a test row
The owner got a GitHub health-alert email for a `needs_review` package (`83b7825f-...`) that, on investigation, didn't exist in the database at all — not a status change, the row was fully gone. Root cause: check 3 in [health-check.yml](.github/workflows/health-check.yml) flagged `needs_review` packages the instant it saw them, with no allowance for the closed loop (ADR-0047/0051/0061) that now self-heals most of them within 2-5 minutes via `heal_completed_packages` (every 2 min) and the held-only remediation sweep (every 5 min). It very likely caught the disposable test row from the same day's live end-to-end test of that loop (see "ADR-0051 loop proven live end-to-end" below), which was deliberately broken, held in `needs_review`, and deleted afterward.
- **Fix:** check 3 now requires `needs_review_at` (ADR-0058) to be at least 10 minutes old before alerting — the same grace period `MysteryView.tsx`'s `NEEDS_REVIEW_SILENT_WINDOW_MS` already uses before showing the "finalizing" banner, so the two places that react to a held package now agree on how long to wait before treating it as a real problem.
- **The paired alert in the same report was real:** "Death At The Birthday Bash: A Speakeasy Soirée Turned Deadly" (paid) is genuinely missing its round4 evidence-card image — the auto-remediation worker tried twice (2026-08-01, $0.12 spent) and hit its attempt cap; needs manual regeneration.
- Not changed: checks 4-11 already scope to `is_paid` where relevant or run on a 30-day rolling window; only check 3 lacked any hold-duration floor.

### Verification: ADR-0051 self-healing loop proven live end-to-end (heals, not just holds)
Ran a controlled production test of the full closed loop wired in ADR-0061. Cloned a clean paid package into disposable rows, injected a real `identity_contamination` defect (two characters falsely claiming "my niece"), and set it to `needs_review`. The live 5-minute held-only sweep (`auto-remediate-held-packages`) autonomously claimed it, delegated to `regenerate-child-content`, which rewrote BOTH contaminated introductions to coherent content with the false kin-claim gone (healed — not blanked, reverted, or escalated), re-detected clean, released the claim, and logged `identity_contamination: fixed` at $0.12. The 2-minute sweep then promoted `needs_review → completed` through the existing gate (`package_completion_blocking_defects` null). All disposable rows deleted afterward; the test log row removed so the $0.12 doesn't consume the real $5/day cap. Confirms the loop repairs and releases without a human, bounded by the spend cap, degrading to a safe hold on failure. ADR-0051 layers 1–3 (constraints → gate → self-healing regenerator) are fully closed.

### Feature: wire the child-content regenerator into the closed loop (ADR-0061, ADR-0051 layer 3)
`regenerate-child-content` (ADR-0054) has been a deployed, standalone primitive since 2026-08-01 — gated, re-detecting, audit-logged, but never called by anything. This wires it in, per the exact contract ADR-0054's own Discussion section documented for this pass.
- **`identity_contamination` and `slip_culprit_leak` are no longer escalate-only.** The ADR-0047 worker delegates both straight to `regenerate-child-content` — not wrapped in `runGatedAttempt` (the regenerator already re-detects and reverts internally; wrapping it would race a second, independent revert path against writes it already committed as good). The worker's contribution is narrower: the attempt cap (the regenerator has none of its own), the new concurrency claim, and translating the response into this run's bookkeeping without re-logging.
- **The `meta_text_leak`/`template_artifact` deterministic strip now delegates its own refusals.** Previously, an artifact embedded in real content (not a standalone note) bailed the whole plan with no record of which field was the problem — an uninformative escalate. Now the refusal is captured per-field and handed to `regenerate-child-content` after the free strip resolves; a package can have a freely-strippable artifact on one character and an embedded one on another at the same time, and both get handled.
- **New 5-minute held-only pg_cron job (`auto-remediate-held-packages`)** re-invokes the *same* `auto-remediate-packages` function (no new edge function) restricted to `needs_review` packages and just the three newly-delegatable classes, via two new optional request fields (`only_needs_review`, `classes`). The existing 4-hour full sweep is unchanged and remains the backstop for every class. Chosen over a `pg_net` call from the completion trigger — see ADR-0061 Decision 1 for why: ADR-0055 (same day) already fixed the actual blocker (detector RPCs couldn't see `needs_review` rows), so the only remaining gap was cadence, not architecture.
- **New concurrency claim** (`mystery_packages.remediation_claimed_at`, `claim_package_for_remediation()`/`release_package_remediation_claim()`) so the 4-hour and 5-minute sweeps can't both repair the same package at once. Atomic single-statement UPDATE, no advisory lock (the edge function has no persistent session to hold one across the several RPC calls a repair makes); self-releasing via a 10-minute TTL if the caller crashes. Verified live on a disposable row: claim → true, second claim while held → false, claim after release → true.
- **Shared-cap bug closed:** the worker computed its daily budget once at run start; a same-run delegated repair (which spends against the shared `auto_remediation_log` cap independently) would have left that snapshot stale for any paid fix later in the same run. The worker now decrements its local view by each delegated call's actual reported cost.
- **`package_completion_blocking_defects()` and the gate are untouched.** A repaired package is still promoted to `completed` only through the existing gate/healer path — never on a delegated repair's own say-so.
- **Not run:** the LLM path was not exercised from this session (per instruction — spends tokens and mutates paid content). Verified instead via `tsc --noEmit` (zero errors), two production dry-runs through `pg_net` (full-sweep shape and the exact held-only-sweep shape, both `200`, both mutated/spent nothing), and the disposable-row claim test above. Owner runs the live end-to-end test. Full record in [ADR-0061](docs/adr/0061-wire-child-content-regenerator-into-closed-loop.md).

### Fix: two eval findings against the child-content regenerator, before any live traffic (ADR-0054)
Fresh-eval pass on `regenerate-child-content` (built 2026-08-01, standalone primitive, not yet wired into anything) caught two gaps in the safety invariants the function claims to hold. Neither has shipped a bad repair — the function has not been invoked against production data yet — but both would have on first use.
- **Fix 1 — re-detect gate was missing a class it can itself reintroduce.** `detectorState()` snapshotted `identity_conflicts`, `meta_text_leak`, and `slip_culprit_leak` before/after every repair, but not `self_directed_questions` — despite the function being whitelisted to write `round2/3/4_questions`, and ADR-0053's completion gate blocking on that exact class. A repair that silently reintroduced a self-directed question would have been accepted and reported `outcome: "fixed"` rather than rejected. `list_packages_with_self_directed_questions` is now in the before/after snapshot and in both `stillImplicatesTouched()` and `regressions()` — four classes checked, not three.
- **Fix 2 — the per-field write loop had no failure guard, unlike the Claude-call step above it.** A `remediation_write_field` throw mid-loop (reproduced: throws on `relationships` when the existing value is `null` or a jsonb object, ~7% of prod characters — but the gap applied to a throw on any field) escaped both for-loops uncaught, hit only the function's outermost catch, and returned a bare `500` without calling `revertAll()` or `logRow()`. Any field already written earlier in that same call stayed committed, unreverted, and unlogged — a direct hole in the "degrade to escalate, never ship worse" invariant the rest of the function is built around. The write loop is now wrapped in its own try/catch that sets the same `hadError` flag the generation-step catch already used, routing any write failure through the existing `revertAll()` + `logRow(outcome: "failed")` + response path.
- **Fix 3 — docs corrected to match the code.** ADR-0054 and the file header both claimed a call "regenerates the whole [call-boundary] group, extra fields generated but only the requested subset written." The code has never done that — `fieldsToGenerate = group.fields.filter(f => effectiveFields.includes(f))` means only the requested/effective fields within a group are ever generated OR written; nothing extra is generated, nothing generated is withheld. Both docs now describe the filter accurately.
- **Named follow-up, not built here:** Fix 2 makes a `relationships` throw on a null/object-valued character a clean, logged escalate — it does not make `remediation_write_field` able to actually repair that field in that state. Extending the write path to handle it is separate work.
- **Redeployed** (`regenerate-child-content` v3, `verify_jwt: true` unchanged). Not invoked against the LLM path or live data from this session — owner runs the end-to-end smoke test separately. Still NOT wired into the ADR-0053 gate or the ADR-0047 worker; scope unchanged from the 2026-08-01 build. Full record in [ADR-0054](docs/adr/0054-child-content-regenerator.md).

### Fix: detector could not catch an overview that kills off a playable character (ADR-0060)
The sweep found "The Cognitive Dissonance Incident" (paid) shipped with a `game_overview` naming **Dr. Morgan Cho** as the victim — but the real victim is Dr. Morgan Hartwell, and Morgan/Merritt Cho is a **playable suspect** one of the guests is holding a script for. Roster and bios are built correctly from Hartwell; only the overview blurb has the swap.
- **Why `victim_mismatch` missed it, reason 1:** it tests whether the overview's victim is *absent* from the cast and master_context. "Cho" is present — as a suspect — so the absence test passes. It is built to catch a foreign victim bled in from another mystery and structurally cannot catch a victim who IS one of the cast.
- **Why it missed it, reason 2 — the larger finding:** its extractor requires a bare two-word capitalised name immediately after the header, so any title ("Dr.") or preamble ("On the morning of October 14th,") defeats it. Measured across all packages with an overview: **NULL on 79 of 101 — 78%**. For those, `victim_mismatch` never ran at all, and a detector that returns no hits is indistinguishable from one finding nothing wrong.
- **Fix: [20260802_detect_victim_is_playable_character.sql](supabase/migrations/20260802_detect_victim_is_playable_character.sql)** — a check needing no victim extraction, asking directly: does the overview describe any *playable character* as dead? Character names are expanded through the `A/B Last` gender-variant convention first (`Morgan/Merritt Cho` → `Morgan Cho`, `Merritt Cho`), since that is the form the prose uses. Wired into the shared gate, plus `list_packages_with_victim_as_character()` for the health check.
- **Validated across all 101 packages with an overview: exactly one hit, the known case, zero false positives** — the ADR-0053 bar for gating rather than merely alerting. Post-wiring regression check: 23 packages carry some defect, 22 pre-existing and 1 new; nothing else moved.
- **Scope is ~60% of packages and deliberately so.** The check fires only where the overview contains a death phrase (59 of 98); the other 40% are intrigue/theft scenarios with no death, e.g. the Golden Flamingo. That silence is correct, not a gap: the check is sound *because* "dead ⇒ not playable" is a hard invariant — a corpse cannot hold a script. No equivalent invariant exists for theft, where the wronged party is frequently a playable character. Adding "was robbed"/"discovered the theft" phrases would not widen coverage, it would flag correct packages.
- **A rejected fix worth recording:** loosening the extractor raised coverage 22/101 → 63/101, which looked like a big win until the values were inspected — the extra "victims" were `" But"`, `" When"`, `" Instead"`, `" Game Overview\n\nMaster"`. A coverage metric called it an improvement while the outputs were noise. For a *gating* predicate that would have manufactured false positives.
- **Left open:** `victim_mismatch` being inert on 78% of packages is a separate and arguably larger hole; it needs a genuinely robust extractor validated for false positives before going near the gate. Also unwired: `regenerate-parent-content` can already rebuild `game_overview` from the (correct) `master_context`, which would make this class self-healing. Full record in [ADR-0060](docs/adr/0060-detect-overview-killing-a-playable-character.md).

### Fix: post-snapshot refinements never reached the generator — 3 paid packages affected (ADR-0059)
An audit of every paid purchase in the 35 days to 2026-08-02 found that ADR-0057 (shipped hours earlier) did NOT close the stale-concept class. It fixed selection when a later draft restates the cast; it cannot help when the customer refines in *prose*.
- **Three delivered packages were built from a superseded concept:** Black Swan Society (13 later messages moved the setting to Victorian, renamed the institution off "Morehouse", added a Savannah plot thread — delivered package still said Morehouse, no Victorian, no Savannah); Adelaide Crane (10 later messages established Camille's illegitimacy backstory and Patricia's salad-bar motive — delivered package invented a different, incompatible backstory for both); The Masked Betrayal (the customer's "these must exonerate all but these three suspects" constraint never reached the generator).
- **Why ADR-0057 missed them:** verified against all three — the fixed selector returns the *identical* stale message, because no later message restates the roster for it to find.
- **Why the existing guard missed them:** `snapshotTooThin` (added after Fotini, May 2026) requires `approved_len < 3000`. These are full ~6KB concept messages that are *stale*, not *thin*. Across 8 paid conversations with post-snapshot activity in 60 days it fired **zero** times — it tests the wrong property.
- **Fix: [mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts](supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts)** — send the approved concept message **plus every message after it**, chronologically. Messages *before* the snapshot stay excluded.
- **Why that is safe:** the two failure modes recorded in May 2026 as needing opposite fixes are not opposed — they are asymmetric about the snapshot. Messages before it may be superseded drafts (the Madysn lake-house→circus contamination the narrow design prevents); messages after it cannot be, since the customer wrote them on top of a cast they had already approved. Widening in that one direction carries no contamination risk and recovers all the lost detail.
- **Verified on the real conversations:** "Victorian", "Savannah", "illegitimacy", "salad bar" and "paternity" are all absent from the old payload and present in the new one. Payloads grow 6,026 → 20,467 and 6,782 → 19,888 chars, far below the ~255KB already sent comfortably.
- **Does not repair the three delivered packages** — that needs repointing/regeneration, a separate paid operation. Full record in [ADR-0059](docs/adr/0059-send-approved-concept-plus-everything-after-it.md).

### Fix: `needs_review_at` was never set when the gate held a package (ADR-0058)
Spotted while watching a paid package heal: `status = 'needs_review'` with `needs_review_at = NULL`, two values that should never disagree.
- **Cause:** Postgres fires BEFORE row triggers in NAME order, so `trg_maintain_needs_review_at` ('m') ran before `trg_validate_package_characters` ('v'). The timestamp trigger read `NEW.generation_status` while it was still the caller's value (`completed`) — the gate rewrote it to `needs_review` a moment later, too late. Only the *set* path was affected; the clear path always worked because `heal_completed_packages()` writes `completed` directly.
- **Effect:** `MysteryView.tsx:1235` computes `ageMs = ts ? Date.now() - ts : Infinity`, so a NULL timestamp reads as infinitely stale and the amber "we're finalizing" banner rendered IMMEDIATELY instead of after the ~10-minute grace period. The silent-recovery window had never worked for a gate-held package.
- **Fix: [20260802_order_needs_review_at_trigger_after_gate.sql](supabase/migrations/20260802_order_needs_review_at_trigger_after_gate.sql)** — renamed to `trg_zz_maintain_needs_review_at` so it sorts after the gate, using the same explicit-ordering-by-prefix idiom the table already uses for `trg_00_normalize_generation_status`. Function body unchanged; only firing order moves. The `WHEN` clause is preserved and still correct — Postgres evaluates it at the trigger's new position against `NEW` as modified by earlier BEFORE triggers.
- **Verified on disposable rows** (created and deleted in-session): before the rename a completing UPDATE the gate held left `needs_review_at` NULL; after, it is set. The clear path was re-checked for regression. No backfill needed — zero packages were in `needs_review` at migration time.
- **Named limitation:** renaming encodes the dependency in a sort key, not an assertion. Postgres has no declarative "after trigger X", so a future trigger sorting after `trg_zz_` would silently take precedence. Full record in [ADR-0058](docs/adr/0058-order-needs-review-at-trigger-after-the-gate.md).

### Fix: concept snapshot pinned an early draft when the model renamed its list header (ADR-0057)
The root cause of the 2026-08-01 "Golden Flamingo" complaint — *"the mystery I generated is completely different than the one I'm seeing after my purchase."* Generation had not failed; it succeeded from the wrong draft.
- **Cause:** `approved_concept_message_id` was chosen by testing each assistant message against a hardcoded header allow-list (`Character List|Characters|Cast of Characters|...`), while the characters were later read by a *line parser*. The customer asked for players-as-investigators, the model renamed its section `## Suspect List`, her two revised drafts stopped matching the allow-list, and "latest match" silently resolved to her FIRST draft. Non-null value, so the null-only fallback never rescued it; correct title, correct player count, `completed`, one clean run logged — no error anywhere.
- **Fix: [mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts](supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts)** — one `extractRosterFromMessage()` answers "what cast does this message propose?" (explicit-header section first, then header-agnostic 4+ consecutive `Name - description` lines), and is used for BOTH choosing the snapshot and extracting from it. Selection and extraction are now the same code rather than two predicates that must agree, so the snapshot can never point at a message the extractor cannot read. The header list survives only as the parser's preferred starting point, never as the gate.
- **Deleted `src/components/MysteryChatCreator.tsx`** (290 lines) — carried a second, already-divergent copy of the same allow-list and also wrote `approved_concept_message_id`. Dead code: imported nowhere, and it wrote `conversations.generation_requested`, a column that does not exist, so the call would have failed outright. Build and typecheck pass without it.
- **[scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs](scripts/__tests__/conceptSnapshot.test.mjs)** — 9 checks against the shipped functions (transpiled with esbuild, never a copy), including the live regression. The most valuable is a *negative* assertion that the selection block contains no header-name test, so reintroducing the allow-list as the gate fails regardless of which names are used. Verified against the real customer conversation: old code picked the 17:21 draft, new code picks her 17:35 luau concept and extracts all 8 correct names.
- **Third instance of one bug class in a day** (with ADR-0055 and ADR-0056): one concept encoded as two predicates, in two languages, updated independently. The durable move was to delete the second predicate, not to keep them synchronised.
- **Not fixed:** the sweep for past packages built from a superseded draft is still outstanding. Nor does this address the customer's underlying format request (guests as investigators, suspects as NPCs) — the generator does not build that, which is a product gap, not a bug. Full record in [ADR-0057](docs/adr/0057-select-concept-snapshot-by-parse-not-header.md).

### Fix: question retargeter could not repair the defect the detector flagged (ADR-0056)
The ADR-0055 fix put a gate-held package in front of the auto-remediation worker for the first time — and the worker could not repair it, logging `retarget_questions:round4_questions|redetect_still_flagged|reverted`. Third instance in one day of the same failure: two predicates that must describe one concept, drifting apart because only one was updated.
- **Cause:** the detector (`list_packages_with_self_directed_questions`, and the same test inside `package_completion_blocking_defects`) matches `**to <name>` with a `\M` word-END boundary, so it flags `**To Polly Paradise (self):**`. The retargeter's lookahead `(?=\s*:?\s*\*\*)` cannot cross the ` (self)` annotation, so it could not repair what the detector flagged.
- **Worse than a stall:** revert is all-or-nothing per package, so the worker's *successful* retarget of a second character was rolled back too, and the package escalated.
- **Fix: [auto-remediate-packages/index.ts](supabase/functions/auto-remediate-packages/index.ts)** (deployed v4) — one named `TARGET_ANNOTATION_RX` used in both places the function reasons about a target name. The annotation is *consumed*, not looked past, so `**To Polly Paradise (self):**` becomes `**To Captain Kei:**` and never `**To Captain Kei (self):**`. The already-targeted scan stops its capture before `(` so an annotated name registers as the real person.
- **[scripts/__tests__/retargetQuestions.test.mjs](scripts/__tests__/retargetQuestions.test.mjs)** — reads the pattern *out of the live source* rather than restating it (a script that restates the regex passes while the source drifts — exactly how all three of these survived) and asserts the one-directional invariant: whatever the detector flags, the retargeter must be able to repair. Matching more is harmless; matching less is the deadlock.
- **Two known gaps left open on purpose**, both reported by the script rather than silently fixed: prefix names (a character named `Polly` matches inside `**To Polly Paradise:**` — a detector false positive, verified zero production packages affected) and multi-space (`**To   Name:**` is never detected, since the detector hardcodes one space). Closing either means tightening the detector, which *reduces* detection — a real trade-off deserving its own decision per ADR-0053's "the bar for block is higher than the bar for alert."
- **Limitation now documented:** retargeting is label-only, so a body naming its target's own facts follows the label to someone it no longer fits. That is why the live customer's package was hand-edited rather than left to the worker. Full record in [ADR-0056](docs/adr/0056-align-retargeter-with-self-directed-question-detector.md).

### Fix: auto-remediation worker could not see the packages the completion gate held (ADR-0055)
ADR-0053 (shipped the previous day) added `self_directed_question` to the pre-completion gate on the stated grounds that the class "is fixed post-completion by the live ADR-0047 worker." That premise was false as shipped: the gate sets `generation_status.status = 'needs_review'`, but all eight `list_packages_*()` detector RPCs — the way the worker finds work — filtered on `= 'completed'`. The gate's own action made the package invisible to the worker meant to heal it, and since nothing else clears the flag, `MysteryView`'s stale-needs-review banner (>10 min) became permanent.
- **Fix: [20260802_widen_detector_rpcs_to_needs_review.sql](supabase/migrations/20260802_widen_detector_rpcs_to_needs_review.sql)** — widens the status predicate on all eight detector RPCs to `IN ('completed', 'needs_review')`. Applied to all eight rather than just the one that fired, because the bug is in the shared assumption: a gate-held package is by definition one with a detected defect, so it is the most deserving of detector attention, not the least. No change to the worker, the gate, or the crons — the rest of the chain already works (`heal_completed_packages()` re-checks the blocking-defects function every 2 min and promotes back to `completed` once clean).
- **Applied programmatically** from `pg_get_functiondef()` with a string replacement on the predicate, so every function body is preserved byte-for-byte apart from that predicate, plus an assertion that exactly 8 functions were rewritten — a future reword fails the migration loudly instead of silently under-applying.
- **Side effect, intended:** the 6-hourly health check shares these RPCs, so `needs_review` packages that were previously invisible to it now surface. The four hold-only classes (`meta_text_leak`, `victim_mismatch`, `slip_culprit_leak`, `identity_conflict`) are exactly the ones needing a human, and the old filter hid them from the alerting that would say so.
- **Found via a customer recovery**, not a sweep: package `33671764-71f9-488a-bed7-9afc712b0051` was the first generation to run after ADR-0053 shipped, and hit the deadlock immediately — `package_completion_blocking_defects()` returned two defects while `list_packages_with_self_directed_questions()` returned zero rows. Full record in [ADR-0055](docs/adr/0055-widen-detector-rpcs-to-gate-held-packages.md).

### Fix: customer package rebuilt from the concept she actually approved
"The Case Of The Stolen Golden Flamingo" (paid, conversation `a027af70-39b7-4e87-aa4e-8be295322447`) was generated from the **first** draft of the customer's concept rather than her final one — she received an entirely different mystery from the one she approved in chat, and emailed to say so.
- **Cause:** the edge function's concept auto-snapshot ([mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts:340-360](supabase/functions/mystery-webhook-trigger/index.ts#L340)) picks the *latest* assistant message matching a hardcoded header allow-list. Her revision made the AI rename the section from `## Character List` to `## Suspect List`, which is not in the list — so "latest match" silently fell back to the first draft. The written value is non-null, so nothing downstream corrected it. Failure is completely silent: right title, right player count, no error, one clean run logged in `child_generation_attempts`.
- **Recovery:** repointed `approved_concept_message_id` at the final concept, reset `generation_status`/`generation_completed_at`, retriggered generation. Old package and characters backed up to `temp-files/` (gitignored) first. Rebuild produced the correct luau cast and plot.
- **Code fix not yet shipped** — the header allow-list is the shallow patch; the durable fix is to stop keying on header text and instead take the latest message that parses into ≥4 numbered character lines. Tracked in `00_INBOX/concept-snapshot-wrong-message-2026-08-02-mystery-maker.md` with a sweep of recent purchases still outstanding.

## 2026-08-01

### Feature: Child-content regenerator deployed — ADR-0051 layer 3 (ADR-0054)
The keystone ADR-0051 named: turns the ADR-0053 completion gate's "hold" into "self-heal" for child-generated defect classes, and gives the ADR-0047 auto-remediation worker a real fix for the two classes it has always escalated untouched (`identity_contamination`, `slip_culprit_leak`).
- **New edge function: `supabase/functions/regenerate-child-content/index.ts`** (deployed, `verify_jwt: true`). Regenerates a bounded set of whitelisted `mystery_characters` fields by calling Claude directly with a prompt mirrored verbatim from the live Child Make blueprint (`temp-files/MM Live - Child (Unified)19-...blueprint.json`) — same G-rules, same JSON-safety rules, same per-style call boundaries — so a repair can't reintroduce the very defect it's fixing.
- **Multi-character auto-discovery:** given a `defect_class_hint`, the function calls the same ADR-0042/0041 detector RPCs `auto-remediate-packages` already uses and pulls in every OTHER character implicated by the same defect instance (a 3+-claimant identity conflict, or several slip-leaking characters, needs all of them fixed together — one claimant alone often can't clear the package).
- **Mandatory re-detect gate, extended beyond a literal ADR-0047 port:** re-checks ALL THREE character-level detector classes before and after (not just the hinted one), and requires no touched character still implicated AND no brand-new defect in any class — an LLM rewrite, unlike ADR-0047's deterministic edits, can plausibly trade one defect class for another, so the regression guard checks for that explicitly. Any rejection reverts every write byte-for-byte.
- **Reuses ADR-0047's infrastructure unmodified:** the same whitelisted `remediation_read_field`/`remediation_write_field` accessors (no new writable surface), the same `auto_remediation_log` audit table, and a **shared** daily spend cap with `auto-remediate-packages` (one $5/day ceiling between both functions, not two).
- **Scope, deliberate:** built and esbuild/`tsc`-validated as a standalone primitive only. NOT wired into the ADR-0053 gate's repair-in-loop or the ADR-0047 worker's escalate paths this pass — the exact call contract for both integrations is documented in [ADR-0054](docs/adr/0054-child-content-regenerator.md) for a follow-on wiring pass.
- **Known gap, named honestly:** the original per-character chat excerpts the live generator used are not persisted anywhere and are not recoverable post-hoc; repairs fall back to `master_context` + the character's own established fields + the brainstorming conversation. Live invocation could not be smoke-tested from this session (sandbox network policy blocks direct calls to `*.supabase.co`); recommended before wiring into anything automated.

### Feature: Completion gate extended to reliable content-quality defects — ADR-0051 layer 2 executed (ADR-0053)
Second execution of ADR-0051's sequencing, right after layer 1 (below). Extends `package_completion_blocking_defects()` — the single shared function ADR-0049 built, already enforced by the pre-completion trigger and both recovery crons — to also block on the four reliable ADR-0042 content detectors plus ADR-0041's identity-conflict detector, ported as per-package predicates (not the full-history scan the read-only detectors use) so a per-row completion trigger stays cheap.
- **Fix: [20260801_extend_completion_gate_content_detectors.sql](supabase/migrations/20260801_extend_completion_gate_content_detectors.sql)** — adds `meta_text_leak`, `self_directed_question`, `victim_mismatch`, `slip_culprit_leak`, and `identity_conflict` to the gate. Regex markers and thresholds are ported verbatim from the validated detectors; only the query shape changes. Because all three enforcement paths already branch on `IS NULL`/`IS NOT NULL` against this one function, **no trigger or cron code changed** — the entire migration is one function body.
- **Two exclusions, both deliberate:** `evidence_culprit_spoiler` stays advisory-only (ADR-0042's own validation found a high false-positive rate — gating on it would false-block legitimate paying customers). `missing_evidence_images` is left to the ADR-0047 auto-remediation worker rather than gated — images generate asynchronously and later than text, so blocking completion on them would manufacture a `needs_review` race against normal, successful generation for every package whose images simply haven't landed yet.
- **Interim behaviour until ADR-0051 layer 3 (child-content regenerator):** blocked packages HOLD in `needs_review` rather than self-heal, except `self_directed_question` (already auto-fixed post-completion by the live ADR-0047 worker) and `missing_evidence_images` (excluded from the gate, same worker). Hold-over-ship-defective is the intended interim trade.
- **A bug caught by the disposable-row verification itself, before anything went live:** the `meta_text_leak` package-level check originally appended an untyped string literal to a `text[]` (`_defects || 'meta_text_leak.package'`), which Postgres resolved to the array-concat operator and raised `22P02: malformed array literal` on the first package that tripped it. Fixed with an explicit `::text` cast. Applied to the DB as two migration versions (the original, then a same-session hotfix) folded into one corrected repo file — same pattern as ADR-0047's two-step migration history.
- **Verified live** with disposable rows: each of the five new classes fires correctly in isolation; a clean package (incl. "iron gateway," a legitimately-established "my brother," and a cross-targeted question) produces zero false positives; the ADR-0049 structural checks are unaffected (regression-checked); and a full pipeline test — real completing `UPDATE` → `needs_review` with `victim_mismatch` in `structuredDefects` → both recovery crons correctly refuse to resurrect it → promotes to `completed` once genuinely fixed — confirms the trigger wiring end-to-end, not just the function in isolation. Full record in [ADR-0053](docs/adr/0053-extend-completion-gate-to-content-detectors.md).

### Feature: character_role made impossible to store as garbage — ADR-0051 layer 1 executed (ADR-0052)
First execution of ADR-0051's sequencing: "start here." Traced generation's only `mystery_characters` writer — Make.com scenario `9061052`'s eight `supabase:upsertARecord` character-write modules — and confirmed **none has an error handler configured** (the `onerror` key is entirely absent from the live blueprint). That ruled out the obvious first instinct: a hard `CHECK` constraint would turn a future 502-body write into an aborted, DLQ-parked scenario run for a real customer, strictly worse than today's bug.
- **Fix: [20260801_normalize_character_role_on_write.sql](supabase/migrations/20260801_normalize_character_role_on_write.sql)** — extends the table's existing `normalize_character_data()` trigger (already shape-fixing `relationships`/`secrets` on write) to **coerce** any non-NULL `character_role` outside `(murderer, accomplice, suspect, redHerring)` to the sentinel `'invalid_role'`, following ADR-0050's coerce-not-reject template on the same table family. NULL still passes through unchanged (legitimate for random-slip games).
- **Sentinel, not NULL:** `package_completion_blocking_defects()` (ADR-0049) already treats NULL as legitimate, so coercing to NULL would have hidden a scrubbed 502 body inside that carve-out. `'invalid_role'` deliberately trips the *existing* invalid_role check instead, routing straight into ADR-0049's already-verified needs_review/retry flow — no changes needed to the gate itself.
- **Historical data reconciled:** 21 rows (2 paid, completed 2026-04-22 packages) held legacy uppercase vocabulary (MURDERER/GUILTY/ACCOMPLICE/INNOCENT) instead of the current enum — a genuine customer-facing bug fix bundled in, since `CharacterAccess.tsx`'s role banner only matches lowercase and was silently not rendering for these two packages. Mapped to the current vocabulary (idempotent).
- **Verified live** with disposable rows: a raw 502 HTML body coerces to `invalid_role` on both INSERT and UPDATE; all four valid roles and NULL pass through untouched; a package holding the sentinel is correctly held at `needs_review` by the completion gate and both recovery crons, then completes normally once genuinely fixed; a clean package (incl. an "iron gateway" false-positive probe) completes with no false gating; reconciliation UPDATE is a no-op on re-run; security advisors clean.
- **Make.com root cause not fixed** — same as ADR-0049/0050's precedent, adding error handlers to the eight write modules is scoped as deferred Make-UI follow-up work, not attempted via blind blueprint edit. Full record in [ADR-0052](docs/adr/0052-normalize-character-role-on-write.md).

### Decision: Shift-left generation integrity — guarantee clean delivery, not perfect generation (ADR-0051)
Capstone strategy after two weeks where ~every generated mystery carried ≥1 mechanically-detectable defect. Reframe: generation errors are inevitable (stochastic LLMs + fragile multi-hop chain + ~300 independent fields per large package → "at least one defect" is the default); *delivered* errors are eliminable because every class we've hit is detectable. Target = "zero detectable defects delivered," via four layers: (1) structural DB constraints (make the worst classes impossible to persist), (2) a pre-completion gate over all detector classes (never mark `completed` with a hit — extends ADR-0049), (3) a child-content regenerator (the keystone — turns "hold" into "self-heal" and unlocks the ADR-0047 worker's escalate classes), (4) Make error-handlers/connector-write reliability (root cause, backstopped by 1–2). Detectors + auto-remediation move from front line to backstop. Pattern already proven twice this session (ADR-0049 gate, ADR-0050 normalize-on-write). Sequenced execution starts with the `character_role` constraint. Full record in [ADR-0051](docs/adr/0051-shift-left-generation-integrity.md).

### Fix: Root cause of generation_status double-encoding found and closed at the write boundary (ADR-0050)
Follow-on to the backfill below, whose own header flagged the root cause as unfixed. Audited every writer: `mysteryPackageService.ts`, `mystery-webhook-trigger`, and `api/generation-complete.js` all pass plain JS objects and don't double-encode. The actual writer is Make.com's live production scenario ("MM Live - Parent v49 (Accomplice-Beat Silent-Omission)", id `9106101`) — its Supabase connector's `getTableParams` RPC exposes **every** column, including the jsonb `generation_status` column, as Make field `type: "text"` (no object/collection type exists for jsonb in this connector), so all 25 `upsertARecord` module instances across its 4 parallel routes build `generation_status` as a hand-escaped JSON string, which Postgres then stores as a valid jsonb *scalar string* rather than an object.
- **Fix: [20260801_normalize_generation_status_on_write.sql](supabase/migrations/20260801_normalize_generation_status_on_write.sql)** — a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger (`trg_00_normalize_generation_status`, named to fire before the existing `trg_maintain_needs_review_at`) that passes an already-correct object through untouched, **coerces** a jsonb string that decodes to a JSON object (the Make.com pattern) into that object, and **rejects** (`RAISE EXCEPTION`) anything else — malformed JSON, or valid JSON that isn't an object.
- **Why coerce instead of a hard CHECK:** Make.com will keep sending the escaped-string form until the scenario is redesigned (the connector has no non-text field type to switch to for jsonb — the real fix is replacing the Supabase modules with raw HTTP modules, a full scenario redesign, not a field edit). A hard reject would break the live, paying-customer generation pipeline today; coercion closes the data-integrity hole immediately without that cost.
- **Verified live** against a disposable synthetic row (created + deleted in-session): the exact Make.com write pattern lands as `jsonb_typeof = 'object'` on both INSERT and UPDATE; a non-JSON string and a JSON array are both rejected with a clear error; the normal object-shaped write every in-repo writer already sends passes through unchanged; post-test row count/types (145 objects) match pre-test exactly. Security advisors clean.
- **Make.com scenario itself not edited** — `scenarios_update` wholesale-replaces a 2MB live blueprint with no partial edit, and 25 duplicated write sites across 4 routes made a blind API edit too risky to attempt under this task. The scenario redesign (replace `upsertARecord` with `http:ActionSendData` for a true JSON body) is scoped as deferred follow-up work, logged to the vault.

### Feature: Structural-defect PREVENTION at completion, not just detection (ADR-0049)
ADR-0048 (same day, below) added a read-only detector for the Velvet Viper/Coronation failure class — a raw 502 body stored verbatim as a character's `character_role` (Coronation: also `background` and `secret`, all three holding the identical 121-char error page). Detection alone let Coronation ship to a paying customer marked `completed` before anyone noticed. New [migration](supabase/migrations/20260801_prevent_structural_defects_at_completion.sql) closes the loop:
- **`package_completion_blocking_defects()`** — shared check: any non-NULL `character_role` outside `(murderer, accomplice, suspect, redHerring)`, or any delivered field (package- or character-level, dynamic column scan) containing a raw upstream error/HTML body (`<html`, `<!DOCTYPE`, "bad gateway", "gateway timeout", 502/503/504 + reason phrase — patterns narrow enough that a plot mentioning a literal "gateway" never false-positives; verified).
- **Wired into `validate_package_characters()`**, the existing pre-completion trigger (fires once, on the `generation_completed_at` NULL→NOT NULL transition) — this is the one point every completion path (the Make.com callback `api/generation-complete.js`, the client-side auto-correction in `mysteryPackageService.ts`, and any future direct Make.com write) already goes through, since Postgres triggers fire regardless of caller.
- **Also wired into `heal_completed_packages()` and `promote_complete_packages()`** (both cron, every 2 minutes) — investigation found both bypass the trigger above by construction (neither touches `generation_completed_at`), so without this a gated package would have been silently re-promoted to `completed` by the very next healer tick. Verified live: a synthetic package with a 502 body in `character_role`/`background`/`secret` was blocked at the completing UPDATE, survived both healer functions unchanged, and only promoted to `completed` after the fields were actually fixed (retry flow intact). A clean package — including one whose plot mentions "an old iron gateway" — still completed normally.
- **Root cause traced with high confidence, not applied:** Make.com scenario `9061052` ("MM Live - Child (Unified) v19"), the eleven `http:ActionSendData` "Parse Claude JSON" modules (ids 402/406/410/413/502/506/510/514/518/521/525) all have `handleErrors: false` and no error handler anywhere in the scenario — a 5xx from the `parse-claude-json` edge function is never treated as a Make error, so the raw body flows straight into the character upsert. Fix requires a Make-UI error handler (this project's own convention: not done via blueprint edit); documented as a precise recommendation in ADR-0049 rather than applied blind.

### Fix: Normalized double-encoded generation_status (detectors were silently skipping 18 completed packages)
24 `mystery_packages` rows stored `generation_status` as a jsonb *string* of JSON instead of a jsonb object, so `generation_status->>'status'` returned NULL and the `= 'completed'` filter used by every ADR-0016/0041/0042 detector + the health check silently skipped them (18 were `completed`). Real defects hid there — including "Velvet Viper", whose post-regeneration verification returned a **false-clean** because the content detectors could not see the row. Backfill [20260801_normalize_generation_status_double_encoding.sql](supabase/migrations/20260801_normalize_generation_status_double_encoding.sql) decodes them (lossless, idempotent; applied live). Re-running detectors across all history immediately surfaced previously-hidden defects (identity 1→2; meta-leak and self-q each +1). **Root cause of the double-encoding is NOT yet fixed** — a writer double-stringifies status on some runs, so rows will re-encode until it's found; tracked as a follow-on.

### Feature: Structural-integrity detector — health check 11, escalate-only (ADR-0048)
ADR-0042's detectors read *prose*; nothing read *structure*. "Death At The Velvet Viper" (paid, 2026-07-30) reached `completed` with a 502 HTML body stored as a character's `character_role`, **two** `murderer` characters for one crime, and a gender-duplicated 30-person cast — and every content detector plus the health check reported green. New [migration](supabase/migrations/20260801_detect_structural_defects.sql) adds `list_packages_with_structural_defects(_since)` (read-only, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `service_role`), wired into [health-check.yml](.github/workflows/health-check.yml) as check 11 🔴 on the same 30-day window as checks 6–10.
- **Four sub-checks, validated against ALL history: 6 packages flagged, zero false positives.** `invalid_role` (`character_role` outside `murderer/accomplice/suspect/redHerring`; NULL is legitimate for random-slip games) — 3 hits; `multiple_murderers` (>1 murderer in a predetermined game) — 2 hits; `duplicated_cast` (two characters sharing a surname **and** a byte-identical `**Role:**` line) — 1 hit, exactly the Velvet Viper package; `name_background_mismatch` (a row whose own `**Name:**` line names a different person) — 0 hits, zero FP, verified by construction against the original Grace/Gus Marchand cross-wiring.
- **It found a live defect on its first run:** "Murder At The Coronation: A Royal Scandal" (paid, 2026-07-31) has an **unfixed 502 stored as a `character_role`** — the motivating failure recurred the next day and nobody had noticed. Inside the 30-day window, so check 11 will alert on it.
- **ESCALATE-ONLY by design.** None of these are repairable in place — you cannot synthesise the correct role from a 502 body, choose between two murderers, or un-cross-wire a cast. Regeneration is the only remedy, so the ADR-0047 auto-remediation worker is deliberately left untouched and its handler allowlist unchanged.
- **Two sub-checks investigated and dropped rather than shipped noisy** (same discipline as the ADR-0042 meta-leak tightening): cast-count vs `player_count` flagged **35** packages (`player_count` is the request-time ask, not a contract), and raw duplicate-surname flags every legitimate family mystery. The naive name-vs-background comparison flagged **18** packages, almost all benign — mostly the intentional `Jordan/Jordana Vance` gender-flexible naming convention — and was tightened to the cross-wire form instead.

### Fix: Detector `generation_status` filter was silently skipping 17 completed packages (ADR-0048)
Found while validating check 11. `generation_status` is `jsonb`, but **23 of 144 package rows hold a jsonb *string* of encoded JSON** rather than an object — including the Velvet Viper package itself. For those rows `generation_status->>'status'` returns NULL, so the `= 'completed'` filter used by every ADR-0016/0041/0042 detector (and the ADR-0047 worker's window) skips them entirely; 17 of the 23 are `completed`. The new detector normalises both encodings and is unaffected. The existing detectors still carry the narrow filter — they were validated against a silently reduced corpus. Logged as an open follow-up, not bundled into this change.

### Improvement: Auto-remediation worker re-eval passed — cron enabled (ADR-0047)
Independent re-eval of the blocking fixes returned **PASS**; the worker now runs unattended every 4 hours (`43 */4 * * *`, active). The eval first deployed the committed source as **v2** — the running v1 was still the pre-fix code, so the fixes were not actually live until this ran.
- **The blocking bug is fixed at the behavioural level:** a character `accusations` field with an embedded `[choose …]` artifact escalated as `escalate:no_mechanical_fix` with its md5 **identical** across four consecutive real runs. Previously this emptied the field.
- **Content-loss guard + apply-revert confirmed together:** a mid-apply throw on field 2 of 2 reverted the already-written field 1 **byte-for-byte** and logged `…|apply_failed|reverted`.
